nahhas-meani:223-223.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿نِسَآؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
That is, a place of tillage («حرث») for you, just as you say: "This house is a benefit (manfaʿa) for you," meaning a place of benefit for you. So the meaning is: you till offspring from them.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَأْتُواْ حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ﴾.
The soundest of what has been narrated about this is that Mālik ibn Anas, Sufyān and Shuʿba narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir, that the Jews said: "Whoever comes to a woman in her vagina from behind her, her child comes out cross-eyed." So Allah revealed: ﴿نِسَآؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ، فَأْتُواْ حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid likewise said: "Standing, sitting, facing forwards and facing away — in the vagina."
Abū Isḥāq narrated from Zāyida, from ʿUmayra: "I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about withdrawal (ʿazl) and he said: ﴿نِسَآؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَّكُمْ فَأْتُواْ حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ﴾ — if you wish, withdraw, and if you wish, do not withdraw."
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ﴾ means "whenever you wish."
And its meaning is "from wherever you wish," that is, from whichever direction you wish.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The basic sense of «حرث» (tillage) is what comes forth from what is sown, and Allah the Exalted creates the child from the sperm-drop.
* And His words: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ﴾ point to an admonition that they should not go beyond this.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَقَدِّمُواْ لأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾.
That is, obedience.
And it was said: in seeking offspring.

nahhas-meani:224-224.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ تَجْعَلُواْ ٱللَّهَ عُرْضَةً لأَيْمَانِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ وَتُصْلِحُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said — and this is Saʿīd's wording: It is the man who swears that he will not do good, nor pray, nor make peace; then it is said to him: "Do good," and he says: "I have sworn."
The implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic is: "out of dislike that (karāhata an) you do good."

nahhas-meani:225-225.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿لاَّ يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱلَّلغْوِ فِيۤ أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾.
There are several views on it:
Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās said — and this is Abū Hurayra's wording: The idle oath (laghw al-yamīn) is a person's swearing about a thing, thinking that it is [as] he swore about it, and then it turns out to be otherwise.
Al-Ḥasan held this view, as did Mujāhid, Manṣūr and Mālik.
Mālik and Shuʿba narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha that she said: "The idle oath is a person's saying: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes indeed, by Allah.'" Al-Shaʿbī held this view.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It is the man who swears about a lawful matter, forbidding it [to himself].
Zayd ibn Aslam stated a fourth view; he said: It is a man's saying: "May Allah blind my sight if I do not do such-and-such," "May Allah strip me of my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow." Were He to take him to account for this, He would leave him nothing.
﴿وَلَـٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾.
He said: Such as a man's saying: "He is an unbeliever, he is a polytheist" — He does not take him to account until that comes from his own [heart].
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of these views is the view of ʿĀʾisha, because Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, saying: My father informed me from ʿĀʾisha, concerning His words ﴿لاَّ يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱلَّلغْوِ فِيۤ أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾, that she said: It was revealed concerning a man's saying: "No, by Allah," and "Yes indeed, by Allah."
So this is a report from her of her knowledge of the actual matter about which this verse was revealed.
And laghw in the language is what is disregarded (yulghā): a man says in anger and haste "No, by Allah" and "Yes indeed, by Allah," among the things his heart has not bound itself to.
The view of Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās also does not fall outside this, because when the swearer swears about a thing, thinking it is the thing he swore about, he did not intend anything other than what he swore about, yet he swears to its opposite; and both oaths are laghw. And Allah knows best.
As for the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, it is far-fetched, because abandoning what he swore about — something lawful which he forbids [to himself] — if he makes expiation, he is not a sinner who is pardoned; rather he is rewarded, [accepting] the command of Allah.
And the view of Zayd ibn Aslam is impossible, because a man's saying "May Allah blind my sight" is a supplication, not an oath.
And it was said: laghw is that whose sin has been cancelled (ulghiya).
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾.
That is, He has forgiven you the idle oath, and has not commanded you to make expiation for it, nor imposed a punishment on you. ﴿حليمٌ﴾ (Forbearing) in His refraining from hastening punishment upon one who swore falsely. And Allah knows best.
* And His words: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾.
Ibn Jurayḥ [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably Ibn Jurayj] said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ: I said about something I intend: "By Allah, I will not do it," and I did not bind it (lam aʿqidhu). He said: That too is among what your hearts have earned, and he recited: ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخُِكُمْ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: And the binding (taʿqīd) is: "By Allah, besides whom there is no god."
So ʿAṭāʾ explained that the statement "By Allah, I will not do [it]" is among what the heart has earned and that expiation is due for it, and that the binding of the oath is "By Allah, besides whom there is no god."
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾ — he said: by what you have bound yourselves to.

nahhas-meani:226-226.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic is: "for those who swear off separating from their wives," that is, [swear] that they will separate from their wives.
ʿAṭāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The īlāʾ (oath of abstention) of the people of the Jāhiliyya was a year, or years, or more than that; so Allah set a time limit of four months for them. Whoever among them made an īlāʾ of less than four months, it is not an īlāʾ."
And in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās: they used to do that when they did not want the woman yet disliked that anyone else should marry her; they would make īlāʾ, that is, swear that they would not approach her.
So Allah made the term by which what the man has [in mind] regarding the woman becomes known four months; and when it is complete and he has not "returned" (lam yafiʾ) — that is, has not returned to intercourse with his wife — she is divorced, according to the view of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās.
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read: ﴿فَإِنْ فَاءوا فِيهنَّ﴾.
And some people said: He is not one who makes īlāʾ (mūlī) until he swears for more than four months; then, when four months are complete for him and he has not had intercourse, thereby breaking his oath, he is held to either intercourse or divorce.
This was narrated from ʿUmar, ʿAlī and Abū al-Dardāʾ. Mālik narrated it from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar.
Masrūq and al-Shaʿbī said: al-fayʾ is intercourse.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-fayʾ in the language is returning, so on this [view] it is returning to having intercourse with her. And ṭalāq (divorce) is taken from their saying: aṭlaqtu al-nāqata fa-ṭalaqat ("I released the she-camel and she went free") when you let her loose from a hobble or a fetter. It is as though the married woman is bound to her husband, so when he separates from her he releases her from a bond.
This is indicated by [the expression] umlika fulān, which means: he was made to possess the woman. However, what is used is: uṭliqat al-nāqatu fa-ṭalaqat ("the she-camel was released and went free"), and ṭulliqat al-marʾatu fa-ṭalaqat, wa-ṭalaqat ("the woman was divorced and became divorced").
[Translator's note: the last form is written «وطَلَقَتْ» alongside «فَطَلُقَتْ», i.e. the two vowelings ṭalaqat / ṭaluqat.]

nahhas-meani:228-228.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَٱلْمُطَلَّقَاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ ثَلاَثَةَ قُرُوۤءٍ﴾.
ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Muʿādh, Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-Dardāʾ and Abū Mūsā said: three menstrual periods.
ʿĀʾisha, Zayd ibn Thābit and Ibn ʿUmar said: and three periods of purity.
In support of the first view it is argued that the waiting period (ʿidda) of the slave-woman is two menstrual periods, and she is only liable for half of what the free woman is liable for; and ʿUmar said: "If I were able to make it one menstrual period and a half — [of a] menstrual period — I would have done so."
And al-qurʾ according to the lexicographers is "time," so it applies to both together. [Translator's note: the source has «يقمع لهما», evidently for «يقع لهما» "applies to both".]
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: It is said aqraʾati al-rīḥu when the wind blows at its [due] time.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Salama narrated to me, saying: Maḥmūd ibn Ḥassān the grammarian narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Hishām narrated to us from Abū Zayd the grammarian, from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: Among the Arabs are those who call menstruation qurʾ, and among them are those who call purity qurʾ, and among them are those who combine them both and call menstruation together with purity a qurʾ.
* And His words: ﴿وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِيۤ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ﴾.
Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means pregnancy and menstruation.
Qatāda said: It was known that among them were concealers, who would conceal and take the child off to someone else, so Allah forbade them that.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ﴾.
This does not mean that concealing is permitted to one who does not believe; rather, it is like your saying: "If you are a believer, then avoid sin," that is, faith ought to [restrain] you from it, because it is not among the deeds of the people of faith.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾.
[Ibrāhīm] and Qatāda said: during the three qurūʾ; and the implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic is: [in] the term.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنْ أَرَادُوۤاْ إِصْلاَحاً﴾.
That is, if the husbands, by taking them back, intend reconciliation, not harm.
Yazīd al-Naḥwī narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿إِنْ أَرَادُوۤاْ إِصْلاَحاً﴾ — that is because when a man divorced his wife he had the greater right to take her back, even if he divorced her three times; then that was abrogated, and He said: ﴿الطَّلاَقُ مَرَّتَانِ فَإمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإحْسانٍ﴾.
* And His words: ﴿وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾, that he said: I indeed love to adorn myself for the woman just as I love that she adorn herself for me.
Ibn Zayd said: They fear Allah regarding them, just as it is incumbent on them to fear Allah regarding them [the husbands].
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is that by which Allah has favoured him over her: jihad, the superiority of his inheritance over hers, and everything by which he has been favoured over her.
Abū Mālik said: He may divorce her, while she has no say in the matter.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Baqara, which is Medinan. Among [what we treat] in it:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿الۤمۤ﴾.
The people of exegesis and the lexicographers differed over the meaning of ﴿الۤمۤ﴾ and what resembles it. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghdādī narrated to us in al-Ramla, saying: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Raqqī Abū ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to us from ʿAṭāʾ from Abū al-Ḍuḥā from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿الۤمۤ﴾, that he said: "I am Allah, I know best"; ﴿الۤمۤ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel reports have ﴿الۤر﴾ here] "I am Allah, I see"; ﴿الۤمۤصۤ﴾ "I am Allah, I distinguish."
Abū al-Yaqẓān related the like of it from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.
The explanation of this view is that the alif conveys the meaning of "أنا" (I), the lām conveys the name of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and the mīm conveys the meaning of "أعلم" (I know best).
I saw Abū Isḥāq inclining to this view, and he would say: I hold that each letter of them conveys a meaning.
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿الۤمۤصۤ﴾, ﴿كۤهيعۤصۤ﴾, ﴿طه﴾, ﴿طسۤ﴾, ﴿طسۤمۤ﴾, ﴿يسۤ﴾, ﴿صۤ﴾, ﴿حـمۤ عۤسۤقۤ﴾, ﴿قۤ﴾, ﴿نۤ وَٱلْقَلَمِ﴾ and things like these are an oath by which Allah swore, and they are among the names of Allah the Exalted.
Ibn ʿUlayya related from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ from ʿIkrima, who said: ﴿الۤمۤ﴾ is an oath.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Maʿmar informed us from Qatāda concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿الۤمۤ﴾, that he said: It is one of the names of the Qurʾān.
Two views are related from Mujāhid:
Abū ʿUbayd said: Abū Mahdī [Translator's note: so in the source; probably Ibn Mahdī] narrated to us from Sufyān from Khuṣayf or someone else — so he said — from Mujāhid, who said: in all of it, they are the openings of the sūras.
And the other view: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated it to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Baḥr narrated to me, saying: Mūsā narrated to us from Shibl from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿الۤمۤ﴾ is one of the names of the Qurʾān.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said — and it is his preferred view — it is related from one of the early generations (the Salaf) that he said: they are a call to attention (tanbīh).
Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: they are an opening of speech.
Quṭrub holds that they were brought because [the unbelievers] used to turn away on hearing the Qurʾān; so when they heard ﴿الۤمۤ﴾ and ﴿الۤمۤصۤ﴾ they found this expression strange, and when they fell silent to listen to him ﷺ, he turned to them with the composed Qurʾān, so that it might settle in their hearing and their ears and establish the proof against them.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is: these letters, O Muḥammad, are that Book.
Abū Isḥāq said: If it were as he said, it would have to be always followed by ﴿ذَلِكَ الكِتَابُ﴾ or something resembling it.
These views are close to one another, because it is possible that they are names of the sūra and contain the meaning of a call to attention.
As for the oath, it is not permissible, because of a reason in Arabic grammar that rules it out.
The clearest of these views are:
the first view of Mujāhid, that they are the openings of the sūras, and likewise the view of whoever said they are a call to attention, and the view of whoever said they are an opening of speech. They did not explain that further than this, because that was not the way of the earliest generations.
Rather, the rest of the speech from them is in summary form, and then the people of reasoning interpret it according to what the meaning requires.
The meaning of "opening of speech" and "call to attention" is that they are in the position of "ها" in calling attention and "يا" in the vocative; and Allah the Exalted knows best what He intended.
Some scholars refrained from speaking about them and their like, so that al-Shaʿbī said: Allah the Exalted has a secret in every Book, and His secret in the Qurʾān is the openings of the sūras.
Abū Ḥātim said: We have not found the disconnected letters in the Qurʾān except at the beginnings of sūras, and we do not know what Allah the Exalted intended by them.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ذَلِكَ ٱلْكِتَابُ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾.
Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ related from ʿIkrima, who said: ﴿ذَلِكَ ٱلْكِتَابُ﴾ means "this Book"; and so is the view of Abū ʿUbayda. Abū al-ʿAbbās rejected it, saying: because "ذَلِكَ" is for what is distant and "ذَا" for what is near, so if one of them is put in place of the other, the meaning is reversed. He said: Rather the meaning is: this Qurʾān is that Book by which you used to seek victory over those who disbelieved.
Al-Kisāʾī said: It is as if the reference is [to the Qurʾān that is in heaven], the speech is from heaven, while the Book and the Messenger are on earth; so He said: That is the Book, O Muḥammad.
Ibn Kaysān said: And this is good.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is like your saying to a man while he is talking to you: "That, by Allah, is the truth"; in wording it is in the position of something absent, yet it is not absent.
And the meaning in his view is: That is the Book which you heard of.
And it was called ﴿كِتَابٌ﴾ because of what has been gathered in it. One says katabtu al-shayʾ, i.e. I gathered it; al-katb is stitching; katabtu al-baghla (I closed up the she-mule) is also from it; and al-katība is the troop whose parts are gathered to one another.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾. Qatāda said: No doubt in it. And so it is in the view of the lexicographers.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: One says rābanī al-shayʾ when I have clearly perceived suspicion (rība) in it, and arābanī when I have not clearly perceived it from it.
Someone else said: arāba in himself, and rāba another, as the poet said:
وَقَدَ رَابَنِي قَوْلُهَـا يَا هَنَـا * هُ، وَيَحْكَ أَلْحَقْتَ شَرَّاً بِشَرٍّ
(Her saying troubled me: "O you, woe to you, you have added evil to evil.")
And from it: "Leave what gives you doubt for what does not give you doubt"; and from it ﴿رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ﴾, i.e. the vicissitudes of time and what causes disquiet.
He, Exalted is He, stated that ﴿لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾, and then said afterwards: ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا﴾.
The answer on this is that the meaning is: and if you are, by your own statement, in doubt — and according to your claim — even though We have brought you what has no doubt in it; because they said as those before them said: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَفِي شَكٍّ مِّمَّا تَدْعُونَنَآ إِلَيْهِ مُرِيبٍ﴾.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
Al-hudā is clarification and insight.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِيِنَ﴾, i.e. those who guard against what they were forbidden.
Al-taqwā: its origin is from al-tawaqqī (guarding oneself), which is shielding oneself from being struck by what would destroy one.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ﴾.
The origin of al-īmān (faith) is affirming as true (al-taṣdīq), and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَنَا﴾.
One says āmantu bi-kadhā, i.e. I affirmed it as true.
So when you say "muʾmin" (believer), its meaning is one who affirms the truth of Allah the Exalted, and nothing else.
It may also be taken from al-amān (safety), i.e. he makes himself safe by his affirmation and his deeds. And Allah is al-Muʾmin, i.e. He makes the one who obeys Him safe from His punishment.
Shaybān related from Qatāda: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ﴾, i.e. they believed in the resurrection, the reckoning, Paradise and the Fire, and so affirmed what Allah the Exalted promised.
Abū Razīn said concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا هُو عَلَى الغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾: he means the Qurʾān.
Ibn Kaysān said: And it was said: ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ﴾, i.e. in the decree (al-qadar).
Al-ghayb in the language is low-lying ground that sinks below what is around it, in which whoever enters it is concealed.
And it was said: everything concealed is ghayb; and likewise the maṣdar (verbal noun).
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلاةَ﴾.
I.e. they perform the obligatory prayer. The Arabs say: "the market stood (qāmat)" and "I made it stand (aqamtuhā)", i.e. I kept it going and did not let it lapse; and "so-and-so undertakes (yaqūmu bi-) his work" is from it.
The meaning of establishing the prayer is keeping it up at its times and not being negligent in performing what it contains of bowing and prostration.
And it was said: al-ṣalāt is derived from al-ṣalawān, which are two sinews in the rump that are moved in prayer.
And it was said: al-ṣalāt is the supplication in it, and that is well known. Al-Aʿshā said:
تَقُولُ بِنْتِيِ وَقَدْ قَرَّبْتُ مُرْتَحَلاً * يَارَبِّ جَنِّبْ أَبي الأَوْصَابَ وَالوَجَعَا
(My daughter says, as I have brought near my mount to depart: "O Lord, keep my father from ailments and pain.")
عَلَيْكِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي صَلَّيْتِ فَاغْتَمِضِي * نَوْماً فَإِنَّ لِجَنْبِ المَرءِ مُضْطَجَعَاً
(Upon you be the like of what you prayed for; so close your eyes in sleep, for a man's side has a place to lie down.)
Al-ṣalāt from Allah the Exalted is mercy, from the angels supplication, and from people it is supplication and the well-known prayer.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ﴾.
I.e. they give charity and pay zakāt, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَأَنفِقُواْ مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّ لَوْلاۤ أَخَّرْتَنِيۤ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Spending was an offering by which they drew near to Allah the Exalted, according to their means, until the obligations of alms and the abrogating [verses] in Barāʾa were revealed.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنْزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
I.e. they do not believe in part and disbelieve in part, as the Jews and the Christians did.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَبِٱلآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ﴾.
It was called ākhira (the last/the Hereafter) because it comes after a first; and it was said: because of its coming later than people. Its plural is awākhir.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ﴾.
Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd related from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: [They are] upon a light from their Lord and uprightness in what came to them from Allah.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾.
Ibn Isḥāq said: I.e. those who attained what they sought and were saved from the evil of what they fled from.
The origin of al-falāḥ in the language is continuance (al-baqāʾ); the believer was called "mufliḥ" because of his continuance in Paradise.
And ʿAbīd said:
أَفْلِحْ بِمَا شِئْتَ فَقَدْ يُدْرَكُ بالضَّعْفِ وقد يُخْدَعُ الأَرِيبُ
(Live on with whatever you will, for [success] may be attained through weakness, and the shrewd may be deceived.)
I.e. live on with whatever you will of cleverness or foolishness. Then the usage was extended, until anyone who obtained some good was called mufliḥ.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
They are the unbelievers concerning whom it is established in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted that they are unbelievers. It is a general expression by which a specific [group] is meant, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿قُلْ يَٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْكَافِرُونَ. لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ أَنَآ عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ. وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ﴾.
And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنَّكَ لاَ تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهمْ وَعَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِمْ﴾.
[I.e. Allah has stamped over their hearts and their hearings and covered them] by way of requital for their unbelief and their turning people away from the religion of Allah.
[And these unbelievers are those concerning whom it went before] in His knowledge that they would not believe. And it may be like their saying: "Wealth destroyed him" and "Wealth took away his mind", i.e. he perished in it and because of it. So it is like His saying: ﴿فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ نَارَاً تَلَظَّى. لاَ يَصْلاَهَا إلاَّ الأَشْقَى﴾, for that is from Allah on account of their conduct regarding His command.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عظِيمٌ﴾.
Sībawayh said: "غِشَاوَةٌ", i.e. a covering.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ﴾.
Ismāʿīl al-Suddī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: They are the hypocrites.
The lexicographers said: al-nifāq (hypocrisy) is taken from the nāfiqāʾ of the jerboa, which is a burrow by which the jerboa exits when the burrow it enters by is blocked against it.
So [the hypocrite] was called "munāfiq" because he enters Islam by word and exits it by conviction.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا هُم بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
So He negated faith of them, because they have neither conviction nor deeds.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يُخَادِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾.
Al-mukhādaʿa in the language is displaying the opposite of one's belief; dissimulation (taqiyya) is called khidāʿ; and it can be from one party only.
Ibn Kaysān said: Because it contains the meaning of rāwaghtu (I dodged), as if he met one thing with another.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلاَّ أَنْفُسَهُم﴾.
I.e. the punishment for that returns upon them.
The lexicographers distinguished between "خَادَعَ" and "خَدَعَ", saying: khādaʿa means he intended deception even if no deception took place, while khadaʿa means he attained his aim.
The preferred reading in their view is "يُخَادِعُونَ" in the first, because it does not take effect, and the preferred reading in the second is "يَخْدَعُونَ", because He, Exalted is He, stated that it takes effect upon them, through what He discloses of their reports, so that what they concealed while displaying something else came back as a calamity upon them.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: In the second "وَمَا يُخادِعُونَ" is permissible, i.e. by that very same deceiving they only deceive themselves, because its evil consequence returns upon them.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
I.e. and they do not perceive that.
[The meaning: the consequence of the deception befalls none but them.]

nahhas-meani:229-229.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿ٱلطَّلاَقُ مَرَّتَانِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿الطلاق مرتان﴾ — he said: When a man divorces his wife twice, let him fear Allah regarding the third divorce: either he retains her honourably and treats her well as a companion, or he releases her with kindness and does not wrong her in anything of her due.
ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: A man used to divorce his wife and take her back before her waiting period (ʿidda) had ended, and that was his right even if he did it a thousand times. Then a man did that repeatedly, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿ٱلطَّلاَقُ مَرَّتَانِ﴾, and from that day people began their count of divorce afresh, both those among them who had divorced and those who had not.
The implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic is: the divorce after more than which [the husband] does not retain the right of taking back (rajʿa) is twice.
And it is narrated that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Then where is the third?" He said: "The release with kindness."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسَانٍ﴾.
That is: what is incumbent on you is retention in a manner known to be right.
﴿أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإحْسَانٍ﴾.
That is, he makes her affair easy by divorcing her the third time.
And al-sarḥ in the speech of the Arabs is "the easy."
* And His words: ﴿وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُواْ مِمَّآ آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئاً إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلاَّ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
This concerns the khulʿ (divorce for compensation) between the spouses.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-khawf (fear) here means certainty.
Abū Isḥāq said: Its real sense, in my view, is that fear of mutual obstinacy prevails over them.
Ibn Jurayḥ [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably Ibn Jurayj] said: Ṭāwūs used to say: The ransom (fidāʾ) is lawful — Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلاَّ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — and he did not hold the view of the foolish, that it is not lawful until she says, "I will not bathe from major ritual impurity (janāba)"; rather he used to say: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلاَّ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ in what He has made obligatory for each of them toward the other, in living together and companionship.
And the meaning on this reading is: unless the husband and the wife fear.
Al-Aʿmash, Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿraj and Ḥamza read: ﴿إلاَّ أَنْ يُخَافاَ﴾, with ḍamma on the yāʾ.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: ﴿إلاَّ أَنْ تَخَافُوا﴾, with tāʾ.
And it was said: the meaning on these two readings is: unless the ruler (sulṭān) fears, and the khulʿ is then a matter for the ruler.
Al-Ḥasan held this view. Shuʿba said: I said to Qatāda: From whom did al-Ḥasan take his view that khulʿ is not valid without the ruler? He said: He took it from Ziyād, who was a governor for ʿUmar and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Most scholars hold that this is a matter for the two spouses.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِ﴾, and He said in another place: ﴿فَلاَ تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئَاً، أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتَانَاً وإثْماً مُبِينَاً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from al-Zuhrī, who said: It is not lawful for a man that his wife should buy her release from him (takhtaliʿa), unless that [cause] comes from her. But if that comes from him — he harms her until she buys her release from him — that is not proper.
The people of Kufa said: He forbade him the dowry (ṣadāq) he had given the woman, in His words ﴿وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُواْ مِمَّآ آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئاً﴾, then He permitted it: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلاَّ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ﴾; so it is not lawful for him to take more than what he gave her.
But there is nothing in the verse indicating that more than what he gave her is not lawful for him.
The view of al-Zuhrī is clear, and His words ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلاَّ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ then explain His words ﴿وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُواْ مِمَّآ آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئاً﴾.
That is: do not take anything from them by force.
And the meaning of ﴿حُدُودِ اللهِ﴾ is what He has prohibited. The ḥadd is that which prevents [one] from daring to commit indecencies; aḥaddat al-marʾa means the woman refrained from adornment [in mourning]; a man maḥdūd is one prevented from good; [and the doorkeeper is called ḥaddād], that is, one who prevents.
And the meaning of ﴿فَلاَ تَعْتَدُوهَا﴾ is: so do not go beyond them.

nahhas-meani:230-230.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا فَلاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِن بَعْدُ حَتَّىٰ تَنْكِحَ زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ﴾.
The meaning is: if he divorces her the third time.
The people of knowledge hold that nikāḥ here is intercourse, because He said ﴿زَوْجَاً غَيْرَهُ﴾ ("a husband other than him"): the marital relationship has already been mentioned, so nikāḥ comes to mean intercourse.
Except Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: nikāḥ here is valid marriage, when he does not intend to make her lawful [for the first husband].
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is strengthened by the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ:
"She is not lawful for him until she tastes the little honey (ʿusayla)."
And from ʿAlī: "until he shakes her with it."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَآ أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ﴾.
Mundhir al-Thawrī narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him.
He said: Nothing in the Book of Allah has been as difficult for me as this verse: ﴿فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَآ أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ﴾. I kept studying the Book of Allah until I understood, and I realised that when the other man divorces her, she may return to her first husband if he wishes.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِن ظَنَّآ أَن يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Ṭāwūs said: "if they think" that each of them will live well with the other.
Mujāhid said: if they know that their marriage is free of deception (dulsa).
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
That is, they know that the command of Allah is true and must not be transgressed.

nahhas-meani:231-231.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾.
"أَجَلُهنَّ" (their term): the time of the end of the waiting period (ʿidda).
And the meaning of ﴿فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ is "when they are near to reaching it," just as you say: "When you reach Mecca, bathe before you enter it."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَارَاً لِّتَعْتَدُواْ﴾.
Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk [Translator's note: so in the source] narrated from Masrūq: ﴿وَلاَ تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَاراً لِّتَعْتَدُواْ﴾.
He said: He divorces her, and when her waiting period is about to end he takes her back again, not intending to keep her, and confines her; that is the one who causes harm and takes the signs of Allah in mockery.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said something similar.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ﴾.
That is, he has exposed it to the punishment of Allah.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّخِذُوۤاْ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ هُزُواً﴾.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan that a man used to divorce and then say: "I was only jesting," and this was revealed.
And Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ:
"Three things, their seriousness is serious and their jest is serious: divorce, manumission and taking back (rajʿa)."
And it was said: whoever divorces his wife [more than] three times [has] taken the signs of Allah in mockery.
And it is narrated from ʿĀʾisha that a man used to divorce his wife and then say: "By Allah, I will neither let you inherit nor leave you." She said: "How is that?" He said: "When you are about to complete your waiting period, I take you back." So there was revealed: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّخِذُوۤاْ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ هُزُواً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is among the best of these views, because it brings the cause for which the verse was revealed. And all the views fall within the meaning of the verse, because of one who ridicules the signs of Allah it is said "he took them in mockery"; that is also said of one who disbelieves in them; and it is said of one who casts them aside, does not hold to them and acts by something else. On this basis these views fall within the verse.
And the signs (āyāt) of Allah are His proofs, His command and His prohibition.

nahhas-meani:232-232.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلاَ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ أَن يَنكِحْنَ أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ﴾.
Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated from the nephew of Maʿqil, from "Maʿqil ibn Sinān" or Yasār — and al-Ṭaḥāwī said to me: he is "Miʿqil ibn Sinān" — that his sister was married to a man who divorced her; then he wanted to take her back, but Maʿqil refused him, so this verse was revealed: ﴿فَلاَ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ أَن يَنكِحْنَ أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ إِذَا تَرَاضَوْاْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿لاَ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾ in the language is: do not confine them.
Al-Khalīl reported: dajāja muʿaḍḍil — a hen whose egg has become stuck.
It has been said regarding the meaning of this verse that the prohibition is addressed to the husbands, since the address is to them, like His words: ﴿وَلاَ تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَارَاً﴾.
It may also be that it is for the guardians (awliyāʾ), and they were addressed with this because they are among those to whom this happens; and the prohibition to the husbands has also already preceded.
The best is that it be for both together, the address being general, that is:
O people, when you divorce women, do not hinder them (lā taʿḍulūhunna).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The real sense of ﴿فَلاَ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾ is: do not put them in straits by your preventing them — O guardians — from returning to their husbands.
You say: ʿaḍala yaʿḍulu and ʿaḍila yaʿḍalu; and from it is al-dāʾ al-ʿuḍāl, the disease whose treatment is beyond capacity, because it is too narrow [i.e. intractable] for treatment.
And the meaning of ﴿وَاللهُ يَعْلَمُ﴾ is: [He knows] what is good for you in it.

nahhas-meani:233-233.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَٱلْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلاَدَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ﴾.
Its wording is that of a statement (khabar), and its meaning is that of a command, because of the obligation it contains.
Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ [Translator's note: the source has «عدالله», evidently for «عبدالله»], from Baʿja al-Juhanī, who said: "A man married a woman, and she gave birth after six months. He came to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and mentioned that to him, and he ordered that she be stoned. Then ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came to him and said: Allah says: ﴿وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصَالُهُ ثَلاَثُونَ شَهْرَاً﴾, and He said: ﴿وَفِصَالُهُ فِي عَامَيْنِ﴾."
And Ibn ʿAbbās said: So when its nursing is taken away, the pregnancy is only six months.
The point of ﴿كَامِلَيْنِ﴾ (complete) is that the meaning is "complete for the nursing."
Just as He the Exalted said: ﴿تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ﴾, that is, [in place of] the sacrificial animal (hady); and He the Exalted said: ﴿فَتَمَّ مِيقَاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً﴾ — because it would have been possible that something else come after this, or that the ten be hours.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ ٱلرَّضَاعَةَ﴾.
That is, that is the time for the completion of nursing, and after the completion of nursing there is no [legally effective] nursing.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَعلَى ٱلْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ﴾, that is, upon the father to whom [the child] was born, ﴿رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ﴾, that is, the provision of the mothers, ﴿وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾, that is, without falling short in maintenance and clothing, and without excess.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿لاَ تُضَآرَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا﴾ as a prohibition.
Abān read from ʿĀṣim: ﴿لا تُضَارِرْ وَالِدَةٌ﴾, with kasra on the first rāʾ.
And it was said: the meaning is: she should not abandon nursing her child in order to harm him [the father] by it, out of anger at the father.
Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read: ﴿لاَ تُضَارُّ وَالِدَةٌ﴾ in the nominative (marfūʿ), as a statement (khabar) carrying the sense of obligation.
Yūnus narrated from al-Ḥasan, who said: He says: "She should not harm her husband by saying, 'I will not nurse him,' and he should not harm her by taking him away from her while she says, 'I will nurse him.'"
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَعَلَى ٱلْوَارِثِ مِثْلُ ذٰلِكَ﴾.
Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "And upon the heir [it is] not to cause harm."
The same is narrated from al-Shaʿbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
And it is narrated from ʿUmar, al-Ḥusayn ibn Ṣāliḥ [Translator's note: so in the source; the known jurist is al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ] and Ibn Shubruma:
﴿وَعَلَى ٱلْوَارِثِ مِثْلُ ذٰلِكَ﴾, that is, the clothing and the nursing.
And it is narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: the heir is the child; if he has no property, then [it is] upon his agnates (ʿaṣaba); otherwise the woman is compelled to nurse him.
[Abū Jaʿfar said]: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī claimed that the most correct of the views is the view of Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb and those who held his view: that by "the heir" is meant the newborn himself, and that ﴿مِثْلُ ذٰلِكَ﴾ means the like of what was upon his father — the provision of his mother and her clothing in a reasonable manner — if she is among the needy, being chronically ill, with no trade and no husband; and if she is among the wealthy and healthy, then the like of what his father [owed] her of the wage for nursing. And it cannot be other than this except by a clear proof, because the apparent sense is so.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is clearer, because it is the father who is mentioned with maintenance in [various] places, as He said: ﴿وإنْ كُنَّ أُولاَتٍ حَمْلٍ فَأنْفِقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾; and likewise maintenance of his child is obligatory upon him as long as it is small, just as it is obligatory upon him as long as it is nursing.
Then Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions said: ﴿وَعَلَى ٱلْوَارِثِ مِثْلُ ذٰلِكَ﴾, that is, the nursing, the clothing and the provision, if he is a relative within the prohibited degrees (dhū raḥim muḥarram).
But that is not in the Qurʾān.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِنْ أَرَادَا فِصَالاً عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, weaning before the two years.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The basic sense of fiṣāl in the language is separation, and the meaning of ﴿عن تراضٍ﴾ is: by mutual consent of the two parents and consultation, so that it takes place without either of them harming the child.
Then He said: ﴿فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾, that is, there is no sin.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِنْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن تَسْتَرْضِعُوۤاْ أَوْلاَدَكُمْ﴾.
That is, to seek wet-nurses among a people for them.
Abū Isḥāq said: that is, [to seek] for your children [a nurse] other than the mother.
﴿فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا سَلَّمْتُم مَّآ آتَيْتُم﴾, that is, when you have handed over what you gave, by refraining from harm.
Mujāhid said: when you have handed over the reckoning of what the child was nursed for.

nahhas-meani:285-285.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَلاۤئِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read it as ﴿وَكتَابِهِ﴾ and said: "كتاب" is more than "كُتُب" — he takes it to be a generic noun (ism jins).
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّن رُّسُلِهِ﴾.
It is related from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar that they read it as ﴿لاَ يُفَرِّقُ﴾, meaning: each one does not make a distinction, i.e. the Messenger and the believers do not make a distinction between any of His messengers.
Whoever reads it with the nūn, the meaning in his view is: they said, "We make no distinction between any of His messengers," i.e. we do not believe in some and disbelieve in others.
What indicates the nūn is "رَبَّنَا".
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَقَالُواْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ﴾ [285].
The meaning of "غُفْرَانَك" is: forgive us with forgiveness (ighfir lanā ghufrānan).

nahhas-meani:286-286.t: Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was revealed in Medina.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضاً﴾
[Al-Suddī related from Abū Mālik, and from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is saying: in their hearts is doubt.]
[Someone else said: The sickness is hypocrisy and showing off; sickness is in the body just as blindness is in the heart; and one says "so-and-so fell sick" when an ailment has struck him in his body.
If it is asked: By what did the sickness strike them? It is said: This was done to them as a punishment. And it was said: The sickness struck them through the sending down of the Qurʾān, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإذَا مَا أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ أَيُّكُمْ زَادَتْهُ هَذِهِ إيْمَاناً؟ فَأمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَزَادَتْهُمْ إيمَانَاً وَهُمْ يَسْتَبشِرُونَ. وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْسَاً إِلَى رِجْسِهِمْ وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ﴾.]
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلَهُم عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾
One says ālama when something causes pain, and it is muʾlim and alīm; al-alam is pain; the plural of "alīm" is ālām, like ashrāf; and al-alīm is the intensely painful.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾.
Abū Ḥātim said: I.e. because of their accusing the messengers of lying [Translator's note: i.e. reading «يُكَذِّبُونَ»], their rejection of Allah, and their denying His signs. He said: And whoever reads it without doubling [Translator's note: «يَكْذِبُونَ»], the meaning in his view is: because of their lying and their saying "we believe" while they did not believe, for that is a lie.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لاَ تُفْسِدُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that they said: "We are only reformers, and corruption is not our habit."
And the other: that they said: "This which you call corruption is, in our view, reform."

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
The meaning of "أَلاَ" is a call to attention (tanbīh), as the poet said:
أَلاَ إِنَّ هَذا الدَّهْرَ يَومٌ وَلَيْلَةٌ * وَلَيْسَ عَلَى شَيءٍ قَويمٍ بِمُسْتَمِرّ
(Lo! this time is but a day and a night, and it does not keep to any one upright course.)
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
Ibn Kaysān said: It may be said: What blame is there (on one who) does not know that he is a corrupter? One is only blamed if he knows that he is a corrupter and then corrupts knowingly!
He said: There are two answers to it:
One of them: that they used to work corruption and display righteousness, and they did not perceive that their affair would become manifest to the Prophet ﷺ.
The second aspect: that their corruption is, in their own view, righteousness, and they do not perceive that it is corruption; and they have disobeyed Allah and His Messenger by their failing to seek out the truth clearly and to follow it.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُواْ كَمَآ آمَنَ ٱلنَّاسُ قَالُوۤاْ أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَآ آمَنَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The people" here are the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.
﴿قَالُوا أنُؤمِنُ كَمَا آمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ﴾? [verse 13].
Abū Isḥāq said: The origin of al-safah (foolishness) in the language is thinness of forbearance; one says thawb safīh, i.e. a worn-out, thin garment.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
I.e. they do not know that the evil consequence of that returns upon them.
And it may be asked: If they are described with foolishness, why is that not an excuse for them?
The answer is: That attached to them only because they found fault with the truth, so they put themselves in that position, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إنْ هُمْ إلاَّ كَالأَنْعَامِ﴾ because of their turning away and aversion, since after it comes ﴿بَلْ هُمْ أضَلُّ سَبِيلاً﴾, because cattle may be turned by their herdsman however he wishes, whereas these are not guided by warning and admonition.
Also: when they declared the believers foolish, they were in that state deserving of this name.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
The answer about it is like the answer about ﴿وَلَكِنْ لاَ يَشْعُرونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِذَا خَلَوْاْ إِلَىٰ شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ﴾.
Asbāṭ related from al-Suddī: As for their devils, they are their leaders in unbelief.
What he said is made clear by His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿شَيَاطِينَ الإِنْسِ وَالجِنِّ﴾.
And "شَيْطَانٌ" is derived from al-shaṭan, which is the rope.
I.e. he is drawn out long in evil; and from it is biʾr shaṭūn (a deep well [drawn from with a long rope]).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾.
So He, Glorified is He, disclosed what they conceal.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ﴾.
There are several answers on it:
The soundest of them is that its meaning is: He requites them for their mockery. So He called the requital of the sin by its name, for the pairing of the speech (izdiwāj al-kalām), and so that it be known that it is a punishment for it and a requital of it, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَجَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُهَا﴾.
And it was said: It is what is related in the ḥadīth, that the believers will be given a light, and they [the hypocrites] will be barred from it.
And it was said: It is that Allah showed them, in His rulings [in this world], the opposite of what awaits them in the Hereafter, just as they showed the Muslims the opposite of what they concealed.
The holder of this view cited as evidence that after it comes ﴿وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾.
And it was said: It is like ﴿سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
These views come back to the first, because they are also requital.
Among the best of what has been said about it is what one explained: that the meaning of "يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ" is that it [their mockery] strikes them, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا ويُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلاَ تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ﴾. [Translator's note: the Arabic «ما بيَّنه أن معنى ... يصيبهم» is terse; rendered as closely as the wording allows.]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾.
I.e. He prolongs them in their overstepping, bewildered. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إنّا لَمَّا طَغَى المَاءُ حَمَلنَاكُمْ فِي الجَارِيةِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: "يَعْمَهُونَ": they waver.
And the meaning according to his view: they waver in their misguidance.
The lexicographers reported: ʿamiha, yaʿmahu, ʿumūhan, ʿamahan and ʿamahānan, so he is ʿamih and ʿāmih: when he is bewildered.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشْتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلاَلَةَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They believed, then disbelieved.
And it may be asked: How did He say "اشْتَرَوْا" (they bought), when one only says "I bought such-and-such for such-and-such" when you hand over something and take something else?
The answer according to Mujāhid's view is that they disbelieved after faith, so unbelief became for them a substitute for faith, and they became like one who sells one thing for another.
And it was said: Since they gave faith with their tongues and refused it with their hearts, they sold this which appeared on their tongues for what was in their hearts; and what was in their hearts is what remained to them, so it is in the position of the price, [while the other] was taken out of their hands.
And it was said: When they heard the reminder and the guidance, they rejected it and chose misguidance, so they were like one to whom something was handed and who bought something else with it.
Ibn Kaysān said: It was said: It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الجِنَّ والإنْسَ إلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾; since their creation was for worship, whatever opposed it became a substitute for it, through their turning away from what they were created for.
The origin of al-ḍalāla (misguidance) is bewilderment; forgetfulness was called ḍalāla because of the bewilderment in it, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَاَلَ فَعَلْتُهَا إذَاً وَأنَا مِنَ الضَّالِينَ﴾, i.e. of those who forget.
And perishing is called ḍalāla, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَقَالُوا أَئِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِي الأرْضِ أئِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾?
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِجَارَتُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ﴾.
So they were put in the position of one who traded, because profit and loss occur only in trade. The meaning is: they did not profit in their trade; and like it is the Arabs' saying "his sale has lost", because the meaning is known.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ﴾.
I.e. by the deed they did of preferring misguidance [over guidance].
And it is possible [that the meaning is]: and they were not rightly guided in the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي ٱسْتَوْقَدَ نَاراً﴾.
Ibn Kaysān said: istawqada means awqada (he kindled); and it may be that he sought it to be kindled from someone else, i.e. he requested it from someone else.
Al-Akhfash — he is Saʿīd — said: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ has the meaning of a plural.
Ibn Kaysān said: If it were so, He would have referred back to it with a plural pronoun, as the poet said:
وَإِنَّ الَّذِي حَانَتْ بِفَلْجٍ دِمَاؤُهُمْ * هُمُ القَوْمُ كُلُّ القَوْمِ يَا أُمَّ خَالِدِ
(Those whose blood was shed in vain at Falj — they are the [true] men, the men in full, O Umm Khālid.)
He said: Rather it is a singular to which a group is likened, because the aim was the action, not likening an individual to an individual; so it became like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿مَا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلاَ بَعْثُكُمْ إلاَّ كَنَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾, whose meaning is: except like the raising of a single soul.
And [here]: like the kindling of the one who kindled a fire.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَضَاءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ﴾.
"ما" may mean "الذي" (that which), or be redundant (zāʾida), or be an indefinite noun.
And the meaning: it lit up for him, so he saw what was around him.

nahhas-meani:189-189.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلأَهِلَّةِ قُلْ هِيَ مَوَاقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلْحَجِّ﴾.
The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that some of the Muslims asked the Prophet ﷺ: Why were these new moons created? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿قُلْ هِيَ مَوَاقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلْحَجِّ﴾.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made them appointed times for the Muslims' pilgrimage, their breaking of the fast, their fasting, their rites, the waiting period (ʿidda) of their women and the due dates of their debts; and Allah knows best what is good for His creation.
Abū Isḥāq said: hilāl (new moon) is derived from istahalla al-ṣabiyy, when the infant cries out [at birth], and ahalla al-qawm bi-ḥajja wa-ʿumra, i.e. they raised their voices with the talbiya. It was called hilāl because when it is seen, people raise their voices (yuhillu) in mentioning it.
And one says uhilla and istahalla [of the moon] — but one does not say ahalla [of it]; and one says ahlalnā, i.e. we saw the new moon, and ahlalnā the month of such-and-such, when we have entered it.
And a month was called shahr because of its being well known (shuhra) and clear.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: It is not called hilāl until it becomes enclosed (yuḥajjir), and its being enclosed is that it rounds itself with a thin line.
And it was said: [It is called hilāl] for two and three nights.
And it was said: until its light prevails, and this is on the seventh.
Abū Isḥāq said: The best view in my opinion is that it is called hilāl for two nights, because on the third its light becomes clear.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَيْسَ ٱلْبِرُّ بِأَن تَأْتُواْ ٱلْبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلْبِرَّ مَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ وَأْتُواْ ٱلْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا﴾.
Shuʿba related from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I heard al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib say: This verse was revealed concerning us. When the Anṣār went on pilgrimage and came [back], they would not enter the houses by their doors but from their backs. Then a man of the Anṣār came and entered from the side of his door, and this verse was revealed: ﴿وَلَيْسَ ٱلْبِرُّ بِأَن تَأْتُواْ ٱلْبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا﴾ — the verse.

nahhas-meani:190-190.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقَاتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ وَلاَ تَعْتَدُوۤاْ﴾.
It was said: I.e. do not fight those with whom you have made a covenant and a pact.
And it was said: Do not fight those who have not fought you.
Ibn Zayd said: Then that was abrogated, and He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ﴾, i.e. wherever you find them, ﴿وَأخْرِجُوهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ أخَرَجُوكُمْ﴾, meaning Mecca.

nahhas-meani:191-191.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ ٱلْقَتْلِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The apostasy of the believer is worse for him than being killed.
Al-fitna originally is testing (al-ikhtibār). So the interpretation of the speech is: the evil testing that leads to unbelief is worse than killing. And "fatanathu so-and-so (a woman)" means she became for him like one testing, i.e. he was tested by her beauty; and fatantu al-dhahab fī al-nār means I tested the gold in the fire to know whether it is pure or mixed.
For this reason it was said of everything you heat in fire: fatantuhu, because by that it is as if tested.
And it was said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾ that it is from this, i.e. they are roasted.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: The view in my opinion — and Allah knows best — is only that they are burned for their fitna, i.e. they are punished for their unbelief, from futina al-kāfir (the unbeliever was led astray).
And it was said: they are tested, and it is said [to them]: ﴿ما سَلَكَكُمْ في سَقَر﴾? And "the punishment aftanahu" means it requited him for his fitna, as you say karaba and akrabtuhu; and knowledge belongs to Allah the Exalted.
One says fatana al-rajul, futina, and aftantuhu, i.e. I put fitna in him, as you say dahashtuhu and kaḥaltuhu — this is the view of al-Khalīl; and aftantuhu: I made him a tempter (fātin); and this is a fresh, tempting [thing] (khaḍir fatin).
Al-Akhfash said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِأيِّكُم المَفْتُون﴾: it means al-fitna, like your saying "take its maysūr (what is easy) and leave its maʿsūr (what is hard)".
Sībawayh used to refuse that the maṣdar (verbal noun) could be on the pattern mafʿūl, and would say: the intended sense is: take what has been made easy for you of it.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلاَ تُقَاتِلُوهُمْ عِنْدَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ حَتَّىٰ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِيهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: Then that was later abrogated, and He said: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لاَ تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: I.e. polytheism. He said: ﴿وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ للَّهِ﴾, and the affirmation of oneness becomes purely for Allah.
Then He said: ﴿فَإِنِ ٱنْتَهَواْ فَلاَ عُدْوَانَ إِلاَّ عَلَى ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: The wrongdoer is the one who refused to say "There is no god but Allah".

nahhas-meani:194-194.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ٱلشَّهْرُ ٱلْحَرَامُ بِٱلشَّهْرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَٱلْحُرُمَاتُ قِصَاصٌ﴾.
I.e. fighting in the sacred month in return for fighting in the sacred month.
Mujāhid said: Quraysh barred the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the Sacred House in the sacred month, "Dhū al-Qaʿda", so Allah gave him retribution from them the following year: he entered the Sacred House in the sacred month, Dhū al-Qaʿda, and performed an ʿumra.
Someone else said: He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَٱلْحُرُمَاتُ قِصَاصٌ﴾ in the plural because He, Majestic is His praise, meant the sacred month, the sacred land and the sanctity of iḥrām.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَمَنِ ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: I.e. whoever fights you in it, then transgress against him: fight him in it. The second was called transgression (iʿtidāʾ) because it is the requital of the first.

nahhas-meani:195-195.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأَنْفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى ٱلتَّهْلُكَةِ﴾.
The soundest of what has been said about this is that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Do not withhold spending in the way of Allah, so that you perish."
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to us from al-Aʿmash from Shaqīq, who said: Ḥudhayfa said: al-tahluka (destruction) is the abandoning of spending.
Al-Barāʾ and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr said: It is the man who commits a sin, then throws himself [into ruin] and says: I will not be forgiven.
ʿUbayda said: It is the man who commits sins and grave sins and then says: There is no repentance for me; so he throws himself with his hands into destruction.
Abū Qilāba said: It is the man who commits a sin and says: There is no repentance for me; so he plunges headlong into sins.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is more fitting, because Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī relates, saying: It was revealed concerning us, the company of the Anṣār. When Allah had made His religion mighty, we said — secretly from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ —: Our properties have been neglected; if only we stayed among them and restored what has been neglected of them. So Allah revealed in His Book, refuting what we had intended:
﴿وَأَنْفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى ٱلتَّهْلُكَةِ﴾
So the destruction lay in the staying which we wanted — to stay among our properties and restore them — and we were commanded to go out on campaign.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So it indicates that jihād is incumbent upon the Muslims. [Translator's note: the source has «وجود الجهاد» (the existence of jihād); probably «وجوب» (obligation) is intended; translated in that sense.]
And it was also said: The meaning of ﴿وَأَحْسِنُوا﴾ is: and spend.
Abū Isḥāq said: And do well in performing the obligations.
ʿIkrima said: I.e. think well of Allah.
Ibn Zayd said: Be generous again and again to whoever has nothing in his hand.
And the meaning of His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى ٱلتَّهْلُكَةِ﴾,
according to what preceded, is: if you refuse to spend in the way of Allah, you disobey Allah and so perish; and the meaning may be: you strengthen your enemy, and so perish.

nahhas-meani:234-234.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجاً﴾.
It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ﴾, with fatḥa on the yāʾ in both [places], and its meaning is: they complete (yatawaffawna) their lifespans, that is, they take them in full. And Allah knows best.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْراً﴾.
"Ten" (ʿashr) is a number of nights, except that it is known that with every night goes its day.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: The meaning is "and ten periods," each such period being a day and a night.
And it was said: The waiting period (ʿidda) of the woman whose husband has died was made four months and ten only because her pregnancy, if she is pregnant, becomes evident [within it].
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: It is said that the child of every pregnant female kicks at the midpoint of her pregnancy, so she is murkaḍ.
Someone else said: arkaḍat, so she is murkiḍa, and he recited:
وَمُرْكِضَةٌ صَرِيحِيٌّ أَبُوهَا * تُهَانُ لَهُ الغُلاَمَةُ وَالغُلاَمُ
(A mare with a kicking foetus, her sire of pure Ṣarīḥī stock, for whose sake slave-girl and slave-boy are made to serve.)
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿أَجَلهُنَّ﴾ is the end of the waiting period.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿فِيمَا فَعَلْنَ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ — he said: lawful, good marriage.

nahhas-meani:235-235.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾.
Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It is that he says: "I want to marry," and he disliked that he should say "Do not get ahead of me with yourself [by marrying another]" during the waiting period (ʿidda).
Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad said: It is that the man says to the woman while she is in her waiting period after the death of her husband: "You are indeed dear to me, and I am indeed desirous of you, and Allah will surely bring you good and provision," and words of this kind.
Sukayna bint Ḥanẓala said — she had been married to a cousin of hers who died —: "Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī" came in to me while I was in my waiting period, greeted me, then said: "How are you this morning?" I said: "Well, may Allah keep you well." He said: "I am one whose kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ you know, and his kinship to ʿAlī, and my right in Islam, and my nobility among the Arabs."
She said: I said to him: "May Allah forgive you, O Abū Jaʿfar! You are a man from whom [knowledge] is taken and narrated, and you propose to me during my waiting period?!" He said: "I have not done so; I only informed you of my standing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to Umm Salama bint Abī Umayya ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmiyya when she had been widowed from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Asad — who was her cousin — and he kept [mentioning] his standing with Allah until the mat left a mark on his hand from how hard he leaned on it with his hand; and that was not a proposal."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾.
It was said: of the matter of marriage.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: that is, in the proposal.
Mujāhid said: that is, within himself.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرّاً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The secret (sirr) is that he makes a pact with her that she will not marry anyone else.
Mujāhid said: It is that he says: "Do not let me miss out on you."
Abū Mijlaz, Ibrāhīm and al-Ḥasan said: It is fornication (zinā).
Abū ʿUbayda said: It is speaking openly of marriage.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: Some people make sirr fornication, and some make it sexual intercourse; both views are mistaken. It is only intercourse in other than its proper way. Allah the Exalted said ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ﴾, and this is not the place for [mentioning] fornication.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said — that sirr is intercourse in other than its proper way — is, according to the lexicographers, as he said. However, what is most likely in the verse is what Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: that the meaning is "do not promise them marriage"; marriage was called sirr because intercourse takes place in it. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] claimed that the most correct of the views is that sirr is fornication, and that the view of whoever said that sirr is his saying to her "Do not get ahead of me with yourself" is not sound, because it is a public statement; and if he meant that it is said secretly, it would be said to him: then it is permitted openly — and no one says this. Nor can sirr be valid marriage, because that only takes place with a guardian and two witnesses, and this is public.
[Translator's note: «مطلق علانية» is rendered "permitted openly" as the context requires.]
And the meaning of ﴿سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ﴾ is "you will mention proposing to them"; ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرّاً﴾: he says to her, "I have had you in mind, and you have become my wife," deceiving her by that until he attains intercourse with her in fornication.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَقُولُواْ قَوْلاً مَّعْرُوفاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is allusion (taʿrīḍ).
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It is that he says to her: "I do hope that we will come together, and I am indeed inclined toward you."
ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلاَ تَعْزِمُوۤاْ عُقْدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ﴾ — until the waiting period ends.
The implied construction (taqdīr) in the language is: until the prescription of the Book reaches [its term]; and it is possible that al-kitāb is in the sense of "prescription" (farḍ) as a figure of speech.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ فَٱحْذَرُوهُ﴾.
That is, He knows the stratagems you employ.

nahhas-meani:236-236.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لاَّ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِن طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: [Touching is] intercourse.
﴿أَوْ تَفْرِضُواْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً﴾: al-farīḍa here is the dowry (mahr).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The basic sense of farḍ is "the obligatory," as [the poet] said:
"كانت فريضَةُ ما تقولُ [قطيعتي]"
(What you say was [my severance] as a binding decree.)
And from it: faraḍa al-sulṭānu li-fulān ("the ruler assigned a stipend to so-and-so").
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى ٱلْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ﴾ — he is the wealthy — ﴿وَعَلَى ٱلْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ﴾ — he is the poor.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said — and this is the sense of their view regarding the woman divorced before consummation, for whom no dowry has been fixed —: the compensatory gift (mutʿa) is obligatory for her.
Shurayḥ said: It is not adjudged against him, because He said: ﴿حَقّاً عَلَى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:237-237.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِن طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ﴾.
Some people said: She has the compensatory gift (mutʿa) in addition to that, as is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr:
every divorced woman has a mutʿa.
Others said: She has no mutʿa.
That is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, ʿAṭāʾ and al-Shaʿbī.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَعْفُونَ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: [The woman], when divorced, gives up the half that was assigned to her.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿أَوْ يَعْفُوَاْ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ ٱلنِّكَاحِ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn Aswad narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr — he is Ibn Ḥāzim — narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us from Shurayḥ, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib asked me about ﴿ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ ٱلنِّكَاحِ﴾.
He said: I said: It is the guardian (walī). He said: No, rather the husband.
Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said likewise, and Qatāda narrated it from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib.
Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAlqama and Ibrāhīm said: It is the guardian — they mean the father specifically.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The ḥadīth of ʿAlī was narrated from Shurayḥ only by "ʿĪsā ibn ʿĀṣim" [Translator's note: written «عيس» in the source], whereas the eminent [narrators] narrated it from Shurayḥ as his own statement, among them al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Sīrīn and al-Nakhaʿī.
And the soundest thing narrated on it from a Companion is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās.
It was read to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām from Abū al-Azhar Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, saying: I heard ʿIkrima say: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah is pleased with forgoing (ʿafw) and has commanded it. If she forgoes, then so be it; and if her guardian, "the one in whose hand is the tie of marriage," forgoes while she is reluctant, it is valid, even if she refuses.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What the context of the speech and the language indicate is that it is the guardian, he being the one who may contract marriage for the woman without her command, as He said: ﴿وَلاَ تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكاحِ﴾; whereas what is in the husband's hand is only to divorce.
If it is said: "In his hand is the tie of his own marriage," this does not fit the first part of the speech; the husband has already been mentioned in His words ﴿وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيْضَةً﴾, so if it were for the husband it would have been said: "or you forgo" (aw taʿfū); and this is more in keeping with the context of the speech —
even though it is permissible to switch from second-person address to a report about an absent person.
As for the language, it requires that when the dowry has been given in full, he is not called
"one who forgoes" (ʿāfin), but rather "one who gives" (wāhib), because ʿafw is only leaving a thing and making it go away. From it: ʿafati al-diyāru ("the abodes were effaced"); and al-ʿāfiya is the wearing away of affliction and its going; and from it: ʿafā Allāhu ʿanka ("may Allah pardon you").
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَن تَعْفُوۤاْ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.
It was said: the husbands are meant by it; and it was said: the one in whose hand is the tie of marriage and the women together are meant by it.
This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is good, because He did not say (وأن تَعْفُونَ), which would be for the women, nor (وأن يَعْفُو), which would be for the one in whose hand is the tie of marriage.

nahhas-meani:238-238.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿حَافِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَاتِ﴾.
Masrūq said: on their times.
﴿وٱلصَّلاَةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ﴾.
Jābir ibn Zayd, Mujāhid and Abū Rajāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It is the dawn prayer (ṣubḥ).
ʿIkrima likewise narrated [from him], except that he added from him: it is prayed between the blackness of night and the whiteness of day.
And it was said: because it lies between two prayers of the night and two prayers of the day.
Qatāda narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Ibn ʿUmar, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: It is the noon prayer (ẓuhr).
And there is a third view on it, which is the most fitting of them:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: Ḥājib ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muṣʿab narrated to us, saying: Abū Jazʾ narrated to us from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, from Samura, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿حَافِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَاتِ وٱلصَّلاَةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ﴾: "It is the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr)."
ʿAbīda, Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār and Zirr narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We fought the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb), and they kept us busy from the ʿaṣr until the sun was close to setting. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, fill with fire the hearts of those who kept us busy from the middle prayer, and fill their houses with fire, and fill their graves with fire."
Zirr said: ʿAlī said: We used to think that it was the dawn prayer (fajr).
And it was called "the middle" because it lies between two prayers of the night and two prayers of the day.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَقُومُواْ للَّهِ قَانِتِينَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Shaʿbī said: («القنوت») is obedience.
Mujāhid said: «القنوت» is silence.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These two views go back to one thing, because silence in prayer is obedience.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā narrated to us: Yaʿlā — he is Ibn ʿUtba — informed us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us from al-Ḥārith ibn Shubayl, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: We used to talk during the prayer; one of us would speak to his companion about what was between him and him, until the verse was revealed: ﴿حَافِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَاتِ وٱلصَّلاَةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ للَّهِ قَانِتِينَ﴾, and we were commanded to be silent.
And it was said: It is the «قنوت» in the dawn prayer, which is lengthy standing.
Al-Juʿfī narrated from Ibn Wahb, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Darrāj, from Abū al-Haytham, from Abū Saʿīd — meaning al-Khudrī — from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Every occurrence in the Qurʾān of [a word from] «قنوت» means obedience."

nahhas-meani:239-239.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجَالاً أَوْ رُكْبَاناً﴾.
Abū Mālik narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: As for ﴿رِجَالاً﴾, it means on your feet when you are fighting; a man prays with [movements of] his head wherever he faces.
Mujāhid said: and in whatever way he is able.

nahhas-meani:240-240.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجاً وَصِيَّةً لأَزْوَاجِهِمْ مَّتَاعاً إِلَى ٱلْحَوْلِ غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ﴾.
Ḥabīb ibn al-Shahīd narrated from Abū Mulayka [Translator's note: so in the source; the known narrator is Ibn Abī Mulayka], from Ibn al-Zubayr, who said: I said to ʿUthmān: "The verse in al-Baqara, ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجاً وَصِيَّةً لأَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾ — why did you retain it, when the other verse has abrogated it?" He said: "O son of my brother, I do not change anything from its place."
Ḥumayd narrated from Nāfiʿ, from Zaynab bint Umm Salama: When a woman's husband died, she would enter a small hut (ḥifsh), wear her worst clothes and touch no perfume until a year had passed; then she would be given a piece of dung and throw it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجاً وَصِيَّةً لأَزْوَاجِهِمْ مَّتَاعاً إِلَى ٱلْحَوْلِ﴾, meaning for their wives. The woman had the right to live in her husband's house for a year; and if she wished, she could leave and observe her waiting period in her family's house, or live on her bequest until the year was out. Then it was abrogated by four months and ten.
Yazīd al-Naḥwī narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words:
﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجاً وَصِيَّةً لأَزْوَاجِهِمْ مَّتَاعاً إِلَى ٱلْحَوْلِ﴾: that was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, by what Allah prescribed of the quarter and the eighth; and the term of a year was abrogated by His making her term four months and ten.
And in the ḥadīth of "al-Furayʿa," the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Stay in your dwelling until the prescribed term reaches its end."

nahhas-meani:242-242.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
That is, so that you may avoid what is not upright — as though the intelligent person (ʿāqil) is the one who restrains (yaʿqilu) himself from what is not upright.

nahhas-meani:243-243.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ خَرَجُواْ مِن دِيَارِهِمْ وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ حَذَرَ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: They were four thousand; they went out fleeing from the plague, saying: "We will go to a land where there is death"; so Allah caused them to die. Then a prophet passed by them and called upon Allah, and He brought them back to life.
[Translator's note: «نأتي أرضاً بها موت» is translated as written; the sense expected is "a land where there is no death".]
And it was said: they were dead for eight days.
Al-Ḥasan said: Allah caused them to die before their appointed terms as a punishment, then raised them for the remainder of their terms.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They went out fleeing from jihad, so Allah caused them to die, then brought them back to life, then commanded them to [return] to jihad.

nahhas-meani:244-244.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَقَاتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: In the narration of Ibn Jurayj, ﴿وُهُمْ أُلُوفٌ﴾ means that they were forty thousand; and this is more likely, because ulūf is [the plural] for many and ālāf for few, even though in each of them what is allowed in the other is allowed.
As for Ibn Zayd's saying that ﴿أُلُوْفٌ﴾ means "with hearts in harmony (muʾtalifa)," it is not known.
The regular pattern (qiyās) for the plural of alf is aʾluf, like aflus; except that they liken faʿl to faʿal in words beginning with alif or wāw, such as waqt and awqāt.
And likewise [the yāʾ], such as yawm and ayyām. And aʾluf has [also] been said.
[Translator's note: this discussion concerns ﴿وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ﴾ of the preceding verse (2:243), though it is placed under verse 244.]

nahhas-meani:245-245.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً﴾.
The basic sense of qarḍ (loan) is what is done in order to be repaid for it, as [the poet] said:
وَإذَا أُجْزِيتَ قَرْضَاً فَاجْزِهِ * إنما يَجزِي الفَتَى غَيْرُ الجَمَلْ
(When you are repaid a loan [of good], repay it; it is the true man, not the camel, who repays.)
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْسُطُ﴾.
That is, He straitens and He makes ample.
And it was said: He strips some people of what He had bestowed on them and gives ample provision to others.
And it was said: He takes the charitable gifts and replaces them with reward, or in this world.

nahhas-meani:246-246.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلإِ مِن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ مِن بَعْدِ مُوسَىۤ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They are those about whom Allah said: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إلَى الَّذِينَ قِيْلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: As for His words ﴿ٱبْعَثْ لَنَا مَلِكاً نُّقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that was when the Torah was lifted, faith was extracted, and their enemy was given power over the Children of Israel. So He sent Ṭālūt as king, ﴿فَقَالُوا: أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ المُلْكُ عَلَيْنَا﴾? — because kingship was in one particular tribe (sibṭ) and could not be in any other, and Ṭālūt was not from it; that is why the objection arose.

nahhas-meani:248-248.t:
