The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَن يَأْتِيَكُمُ ٱلتَّابُوتُ فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAlī, who said: The «سكينة» has a face like the face of a human being, and beyond that it is a light, gentle wind.
Khālid ibn ʿArʿara narrated from ʿAlī, who said: Allah sent the «سكينة» to Ibrāhīm, and it was a swirling wind (khajūj) with a head.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The «سكينة» is a creature the size of a cat, with two eyes that have rays of light. When the two hosts met, it would put out its paw and look at them, and the army would be routed by that terror.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The «سكينة» is mercy, and the remnant (baqiyya) is fighting.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: The «سكينة» is a golden basin from Paradise in which the hearts of the prophets used to be washed.
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ: ﴿وَبَقِيَّةٌ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ آلُ مُوسَىٰ وَآلُ هَارُونَ﴾ — he said: the staff of Mūsā, the garments of Hārūn and two tablets of the Torah.
Abū Mālik said: The «سكينة» is a golden basin into which Mūsā cast the tablets, the Torah and his staff; and the remnant is the fragments of the tablets on which the Torah was written.
It was read to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām from Abū al-Azhar, from Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us from his father, who said: Mujāhid said: As for the «سكينة», it is the signs you know, in which you find tranquillity (taskunūna ilayhā). He said: And the remnant is knowledge and the Torah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is among the best and most comprehensive of them, because «سكينة» in the language is the pattern faʿīla from sukūn (tranquillity), that is, a sign in which they find tranquillity.
And the meaning of ﴿تَحْمِلُهُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾ is explained by what is narrated: that the Ark was with Jālūt and his companions, and Allah afflicted them with fistula (nāsūr); they knew it was because of the Ark, so they loaded it on an ox, and the angels drove it. This is like their saying:
"I carried my goods to such-and-such a place."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً لَّكُمْ إِن كُنْتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
That is, in the return of the Ark after your enemy had taken it there is indeed a sign for you, if you are believers.

nahhas-meani:249-249.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبْتَلِيكُمْ بِنَهَرٍ﴾.
Its meaning is: He will test you; and the purpose of that is that it be known who will fight from who will not fight.
ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: It is a river between Jordan and Palestine.
Qatāda said: The unbelievers would drink and [not be quenched], while the Muslims would scoop up a single handful and that would suffice them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-ghurfa in the language is a palmful or a ladleful, and al-gharfa is a single act [of scooping].
And the meaning of ﴿فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّيۤ﴾ is: he is of my companions.
Sībawayh reported: "You are two parasangs from me (minnī)."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَشَرِبُواْ مِنْهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً مِّنْهُمْ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq narrated from al-Barāʾ: "We used to say that the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Badr were three hundred and ten-odd, the same number as the companions of Ṭālūt who crossed the river with him on the day of Jālūt; and none crossed with him except a believer."
﴿فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُ﴾, meaning the river, and they saw the great number of Jālūt's companions and their own fewness, ﴿قَالُواْ لاَ طَاقَةَ لَنَا ٱلْيَوْمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنودِهِ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُلاَقُواْ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, they are certain.
And it was said: they imagine that they will be killed in this battle because of their fewness.
And al-fiʾa is a group, from faʾawtu raʾsahu and faʾaytuhu ("I split his head").
﴿فَهَزَمُوهُمْ﴾, that is, they broke them and drove them back. It is said: siqāʾ muhazzam (a waterskin creased) when it is folded and dry.

nahhas-meani:196-196.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلْحَجَّ وَٱلْعُمْرَةَ للَّهِ﴾.
It is related from ʿUmar that completing them is abandoning the annulment (faskh) [of the ḥajj into an ʿumra], because annulment was permitted at the beginning of Islam.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama said: I asked ʿAlī about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلْحَجَّ وَٱلْعُمْرَةَ للَّهِ﴾ — what is completing them? He said: That you enter iḥrām for them from the doorstep of your household.
Abū Jaʿfar said: A group of the Kufans held this, and [one of them] said: the mīqāt (fixed station) was set so that it not be passed [without iḥrām]; as for what is best, it is what ʿAlī said.
ʿAlqama related from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: One is not to go with them beyond the House.
Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm said: Completing them is that what one was commanded to do in them is done.
This is as if it were a consensus, because he must come to the sacred sites (al-mashāʿir) and do what he was commanded, and by that his ḥajj is complete.
As for entering iḥrām from his own land, if it were part of completion the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have done it.
Al-Ḥasan said: ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn entered iḥrām from the town he was in, and ʿUmar disapproved of that from him and said: Does a man of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah enter iḥrām from his house?
And it was said: "Completing them" is that the expenditure be lawful.
Sufyān said: "Completing them" is that one enters iḥrām for them intending them [alone], not for trade.
Al-Shaʿbī read (والعُمْرةُ للَّهِ) with the nominative, and said: the ʿumra is voluntary. All the people read it with the accusative. Concerning the meaning there are two views:
Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ṭāwūs, ʿAṭāʾ and Ibn Sīrīn said: It is obligatory.
Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh and al-Shaʿbī said: It is voluntary.
It does not follow from the reading of whoever reads with the accusative that it is obligatory, because whoever has entered upon a work that is for Allah ought to complete it.
It was said: the meaning of al-ḥajj is taken from their saying ḥajajtu kadhā, i.e. I sought to find out such-and-such; so the pilgrim comes to places which he seeks out.
The poet said:
يَحُجُّ مَأمُومة في قَعْرِهَا لَجَفٌ * فَاسْتُ الطَّبِيبِ قَذَاهَا كَالمْغَارِيدِ
(He probes a head wound that reaches the brain-membrane, with a hollow in its depth … [Translator's note: the line is cited for يَحُجُّ in the sense of "probing/examining"; the second hemistich, as printed, is obscure and is left untranslated beyond this.])
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ﴾ means: you are prevented from completing them.
Concerning iḥṣār (being prevented) there are two views:
One of them was stated by Ibn ʿUmar, and it is the school of the people of Medina; he said: It is only from an enemy.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The other view was stated by Ibn Masʿūd, and it is the view of the people of Kufa: that it is from an enemy and from illness, and that whoever is struck by anything of these two sends a sacrificial animal (hady), and when it has been slaughtered he leaves iḥrām.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related the like of it from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Ṭāwūs related from Ibn ʿAbbās the like of the first; he said — and he recited (فاذا أَمِنْتُم) —: Is security anything but from fear?
So a difficulty has arisen in the verse, because iḥṣār according to all the lexicographers is only the illness that holds one back from a thing.
As for [prevention] by an enemy, nothing is said of it but "ḥuṣira".
One says ḥuṣira, ḥaṣran; and of the first: uḥṣira, iḥṣāran.
The view on the verse according to the school of Ibn ʿUmar is that one says "aqtaltu al-rajul", i.e. I exposed him to being killed, and "aqbarahu", he provided him with a grave; and aḥṣartuhu — on this pattern — means I exposed him to confinement, as one says aḥbastuhu, i.e. I exposed him to detention; and uḥṣira means he was struck by what was a cause of the confinement, which is missing the ḥajj.
It has been related from ʿIkrima from al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī, who said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever becomes lame or suffers a fracture has left iḥrām, and he owes another ḥajj."
He said: I told this to Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayra, and they said: He has spoken the truth.
Only Ḥajjāj al-Ṣawwāf related this from ʿIkrima.
The eminent [narrators] related the opposite of this.
Sufyān related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn Ṭāwūs from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās: "There is no ḥaṣr except from an enemy."
Abū Najīḥ related from ʿIkrima that the one who is prevented (al-muḥṣar) sends the sacrificial animal, and when the animal reaches its place he leaves iḥrām, and he owes the ḥajj the following year.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْيِ﴾.
Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿĀʾisha said: From camels and cattle specifically, one thing rather than another.
Jaʿfar related from his father from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: (فما اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الهدْي) is a sheep.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It may be from sheep and goats, and it may be a share in a blood-sacrifice; and this is the position of Saʿd.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَحْلِقُواْ رُؤُوسَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Day of Sacrifice.
Khālid ibn Abī ʿImrān said, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad: until it is slaughtered.
Most of the Kufans said: The sacrificial animal is slaughtered on his behalf on whichever day he wishes within the Sanctuary.
Al-Kisāʾī said concerning His saying ﴿مَحِلَّهُ﴾: The ḥāʾ has a kasra only because it is from ḥalla yaḥillu — where its matter becomes lawful; had He meant the place where it alights (yaḥullu), it would have been maḥallahu. It is only in the sense of [becoming] lawful.
Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضاً أَوْ بِهِ أَذًى مِّن رَّأْسِهِ﴾.
Mujāhid related from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra that when he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, lice in his head troubled him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to shave his head, and said: "Fast three days, or feed six poor persons, two mudds for each poor person, or sacrifice a sheep."
Abū Jaʿfar said: Whichever of these you do suffices for you.
ʿAṭāʾ said: This is for whoever has lice, or a headache, or what resembles them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: In the speech there is an omission, and the meaning is: and he shaved, or applied kohl, or treated himself with something containing perfume, then he owes a ransom (fidya).
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمْ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى ٱلْحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْيِ﴾.
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: "When he is safe from his fear and has recovered from his illness", i.e. from fear of the enemy and from illness.
ʿAlqama said: When he has recovered from his illness.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى ٱلْحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْيِ﴾.
Tamattuʿ according to the jurists of Medina and Kufa is that one whose household are not "present at the Sacred Mosque" performs ʿumra in the months of ḥajj, leaves iḥrām after his ʿumra, then performs ḥajj in that same year, not having returned to his household between the ʿumra and the ḥajj; he has then enjoyed [the interval] from the ʿumra to the ḥajj, i.e. benefited from what one not in iḥrām benefits from.
Al-mutʿa and al-matāʿ in the language mean benefiting, and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ﴾.
The people of Medina said: Likewise, if he performed ʿumra before the months of ḥajj, then the months of ḥajj came upon him while he had not left iḥrām, and he left iḥrām in the months of ḥajj, then performed ḥajj afterwards, he is a mutamattiʿ.
The Kufans said: If he had performed the greater part of the ʿumra's circumambulation before the months of ḥajj began, he is not a mutamattiʿ; and if the greater part remained for him, he is a mutamattiʿ.
Ṭāwūs said: Whoever performs ʿumra at any time in the year, in al-Muḥarram or any other month, and stays until he performs ḥajj, is a mutamattiʿ.
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى ٱلْحَجِّ﴾
he says: whoever enters iḥrām for ʿumra in the months of ḥajj.
ʿAṭāʾ related from him: The ʿumra is for whoever was prevented and for whoever's way was left free; this verse applies to both of them.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from him: Whoever was prevented owes the ḥajj in the following year; and if he performs ḥajj and performs ʿumra in the months of ḥajj, he owes the ransom.
These views from Ibn ʿAbbās agree, and the soundest of them is what Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related, because the flow of the speech is addressed to whoever was prevented; and if someone who was not prevented performs tamattuʿ, his ruling is this same ruling.
On this basis, what ʿAṭāʾ related from him is sound, and likewise what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related, except that the explicit wording of the interpretation is about addressing whoever was prevented.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr said: Tamattuʿ is not what people do today, one of them enjoying ʿumra before the ḥajj; rather, when the pilgrim misses the ḥajj, or his mount goes astray, or he suffers a fracture so that he misses the ḥajj, he makes it an ʿumra; he owes the ḥajj the following year, and he owes whatever sacrificial animal is easy to obtain.
So the interpretation of Ibn al-Zubayr is that it is only for whoever missed the ḥajj, because He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى ٱلْحَجِّ﴾, so the address fell on whoever missed the ḥajj through being prevented. The leading authorities disagreed with him in this, among them "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb", "ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib" and "Saʿd", who said: This is for those prevented and others.
What shows you that the ruling of one not prevented in this is like the ruling of one prevented is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضاً أَوْ بِهِ أَذًى مِّن رَّأْسِهِ، فَفِدْيَةٌ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوْ صَدَقَةٍ أَوْ نُسُكٍ﴾; this is for the one prevented and others alike, and likewise tamattuʿ.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي ٱلْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ﴾.
ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿUmar said: The fasting is for whoever performs tamattuʿ of ʿumra until ḥajj, among those who do not find a sacrificial animal, between his entering iḥrām for ḥajj and the Day of ʿArafa; and whoever did not fast [then] fasts the days of Minā.
Ibn ʿUmar used to consider it recommended to fast one day before the Day of Tarwiya, the Day of Tarwiya and the Day of ʿArafa.
Al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs and Ibrāhīm said: ﴿فَصِيَامُ ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الحَجِّ﴾: one day before the Day of Tarwiya, the Day of Tarwiya and the Day of ʿArafa.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَسْبَعَةٍ إذَا رَجَعْتُمْ﴾.
Shuʿba related from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Nawwār from Ḥayyān al-Sulamī, who said: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ﴾. He said: When you return to your families.
Sufyān related from Manṣūr from Mujāhid, who said: If he wishes he fasts them on the road; it is only a concession. ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan said likewise.
The implied sense according to some lexicographers is: when you return from the ḥajj, i.e. when you return to the state of not being in iḥrām that you were in before iḥrām.
ʿAṭāʾ said: When you return to your families; and this is as if it were a consensus.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ﴾.
It was already known that they are ten. The best of what has been said about this is that, had He not said ﴿تِلْكَ عَشَرَة كَامِلَة﴾, the hearer might have imagined that he was only required to fast three during the ḥajj, or seven when he returns, because He did not say "and seven others".
As one says: "I take from you a dirham on your journey, and two when you arrive", i.e. I take only two when you arrive.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Had He not said ﴿تِلَكَ عَشَرَةٌ﴾, the hearer might have imagined that after them there is something else; so His saying ﴿تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ﴾ is like your saying in a count: "so that makes such-and-such."
As for the meaning of ﴿كَامِلَةٌ﴾, Hushaym related concerning it from ʿAbbād ibn Rāshid from al-Ḥasan, who said: ﴿كَامِلَةٌ﴾ [as a substitute] for the sacrificial animal, i.e. they are complete in the purpose for which they were appointed, and nothing else was appointed along with them; and they are complete in reward, like the completeness of the sacrificial animal.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حَاضِرِي ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The people of the Sanctuary.
Al-Ḥasan, Ibrāhīm, al-Aʿraj and Nāfiʿ said: They are the people of Mecca specifically.
ʿAṭāʾ Makḥūl [Translator's note: so in the source; probably "ʿAṭāʾ and Makḥūl"] said: They are the people of the mīqāts and those beyond them up to Mecca.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of al-Ḥasan and those with him is more fitting, because the one present at a thing is the one who is with it, and the people of the mīqāts and the people of Minā are not so; and the speech of the Arabs regarding the people of Mecca is to say: they are the people of the Sacred Mosque.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So it has become clear that the meaning of ﴿حَاضِرِي المَسْجِدِ﴾ is for the people of Mecca and those adjacent to them, between whom and Mecca is a distance in which the prayer is not shortened; because the one present at a thing is the one witnessing it in person, and a traveller is only a traveller by his setting out on a distance in which [the prayer] is shortened; and if it is not so, he does not deserve the name of one absent.

nahhas-meani:251-251.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَفَسَدَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: He says: Were it not for Allah's repelling the wicked by means of the believers, and His repelling people, some by others, through the God-fearing character of [some of] them, the earth would be corrupted by the destruction of its people.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is what most of the exegetes hold. That is: were it not that Allah repels [punishment], by means of those who pray, from those who do not pray, and by means of those who are God-fearing from those who are not God-fearing, people would be destroyed for their sins.
And it was said: "Were it not that Allah commanded war against the unbelievers, unbelief would have become universal, and He would have destroyed all people."
And this goes back to the first [view].
And it was said: Were it not that Allah commanded war against the unbelievers, their corruption against the Muslims would have been greater.
And it is read: ﴿وَلَوْلاْ دِفَاعْ اللَّهِ﴾.
Abū Ḥātim reported that the Arabs say: aḥsana Allāhu ʿanka al-difāʿa wa-l-mudāfaʿa ("May Allah defend you well") — like nāwaltuka al-shayʾa ("I handed you the thing"). [Translator's note: i.e. the mufāʿala pattern used of a one-sided act.]

nahhas-meani:253-253.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿تِلْكَ ٱلرُّسُلُ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ مِّنْهُمْ مَّن كَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He says: He spoke to Mūsā.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He sent Muḥammad ﷺ to all people.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾.
That is, the clear proofs.
﴿وَأَيَّدنَاهُ﴾ [that is, We strengthened him] ﴿بِرُوحِ القُدُسِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Jibrīl, upon him be peace.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا ٱقْتَتَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدِهِم مِّن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: the meaning is, had Allah willed, He would not have commanded us to fight after the proof had become clear and the evidences made manifest.
And it was said: had Allah willed to compel them to faith, He would have done so, as He said: ﴿وَلَو شَاءَ اللهُ لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الهُدْى﴾.

nahhas-meani:254-254.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنْفِقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاكُم مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لاَّ بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلاَ خُلَّةٌ﴾.
His words ﴿أَنْفِقُوا﴾ mean: give in charity; and al-khulla is friendship.

nahhas-meani:255-255.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱللَّهُ لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ﴾.
That is, there is no god for creation except Him.
﴿ٱلْحَيُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾, that is, the One who maintains His creation and manages their affairs.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾ is the One who does not pass away.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Allah's mercy be upon him, read: ﴿القَيَّامُ﴾.
And ʿAlqama read: ﴿"الحَيَّ" القيِّمُ﴾.
Ibn Kaysān said: al-qayyūm is [on the pattern] fayʿūl from al-qiyām, not faʿʿūl, because there is no faʿʿūl in the language among words whose middle radical is wāw.
Were it so, it would have been said: qawwūm.
And al-qayyām is fayʿāl; its original form is al-qaywām.
And the original form of al-qayyūm is al-qaywūm. And the original form of al-qayyim, according to the Basrans, is al-qaywim.
The Kufans said: the original form is al-qawīm.
Ibn Kaysān said: Had it been so originally, no change would have been permitted in it, just as it is not permitted in ṭawīl and sawīq.
And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَ تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلاَ نَوْمٌ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: [sina is] drowsiness.
And the lexicographers recited:
وَسْنَانُ أَقْصَدَهُ النُّعَاسُ فَرَنَّقَتْ * فِي عَيْنِهِ سِنَةٌ وَلَيْسَ بنائِمِ
(Drowsy, slumber struck him, and a doze hovered in his eye, yet he is not asleep.)
And the meaning is: He is not diverted from managing the affair of creation.
[Translator's note: «لا يفضُل عن» is rendered by its evident sense, "is not diverted/distracted from".]
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
[This was revealed] when they said: "The idols are our intercessors with Allah."
So Allah made known that the believers only invoke blessings upon the prophets and pray for the believers as they have been commanded and given permission.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾, that is, what of the unseen preceded them, ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾, what will be after them.
﴿وَلاَ يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلاَّ بِمَا شَآءَ﴾.
They know nothing of that except what He wishes to acquaint them with, or what His prophets convey as a confirmation of their prophethood.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī reported: wusʿu kursiyyihi al-samāwātu wa-l-arḍu ("the extent of His Footstool is the heavens and the earth"), as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
Sufyān and Hushaym narrated from Muṭarrif, from Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words:
﴿وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
He said: His knowledge. Do you not see His words ﴿وَلاَ يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا﴾?!
This view has been supported with an unknown verse, namely: "ولا يُكَرْسِىءُ عِلَمَ اللهِ مَخْلُوقُ" (and no created being knows the knowledge of Allah),
meaning no created being knows the knowledge of Allah. It is also a solecism (laḥn), because «كرسي» does not have a hamza.
And it was said: ﴿كُرْسِيُّهُ﴾ is His power by which He holds the heavens and the earth, as you say: "Make a «كرسي» for this wall," that is, something that props it up. This is close to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās.
Abū Hurayra said: The «كرسي» is in front of the Throne.
And in the ḥadīth: "The heavens and the earth within the «كرسي» are only like a ring in an open desert."
And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best what He meant; however, «كرسي» in the language is the thing on which one relies, which is firm and whose parts cling to one another. From it are al-kurrāsa (quire) and al-kirs: what is matted together, layer upon layer.
Al-Ḥasan said: The «كرسي» is the Throne (ʿArsh).
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] inclined to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, and claimed that the apparent sense of the Qurʾān indicates its correctness, namely in His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلاَ يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا﴾.
And He, Majestic and Mighty, said by way of report: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيءٍ رَحْمَةً وَعِلْمَاً﴾.
So He reported that His knowledge encompasses everything; and likewise His «كرسي» encompasses the heavens and the earth.
And the pronoun in ﴿حِفْظُهُمَا﴾ refers to the heavens and the earth.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: It does not weigh heavily upon Him.
Abū Isḥāq said: The hāʾ may refer to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and it may refer to the «كرسي»; and if it refers to the «كرسي», it is [still] of the affair of Allah.

nahhas-meani:256-256.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿لاَ إِكْرَاهَ فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Salama — meaning al-Ṭaḥāwī — narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us from Shuʿba, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿لاَ إِكْرَاهَ فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾; he said: A woman of the Anṣār would scarcely have a child survive, so she would swear that if a child survived she would make it a Jew. When "Banū al-Naḍīr" were expelled, there were among them some sons of the Anṣār. The Anṣār said: "O Messenger of Allah, our sons!" So Allah revealed: ﴿لاَ إِكْرَاهَ فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: So whoever wished joined them, and whoever wished entered Islam.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is, and stayed.
Al-Shaʿbī said: [It] concerns the People of the Book specifically: they are not compelled if they pay the jizya.
Sulaymān ibn Mūsā said: It was abrogated by ﴿جَاهِدِ الكُفَّارَ وَالمُنَافِقِينَ﴾. And ʿUmar interpreted it as meaning that a slave is not compelled to accept Islam.
And it was said: one of the people of war (ahl al-ḥarb) who accepts Islam is not to be told, "You accepted Islam under compulsion," because if he remains firm in Islam he is not compelled.
And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِٱلطَّاغُوتِ﴾.
It is narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said: «الطاغوت» is Satan, and «الجبت» is sorcery.
Al-Shaʿbī, ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الطاغوت» is Satan.
Al-Ḥasan said: «الطاغوت» is the devils.
Saʿīd ibn Mūsā narrated to us in Qarqīsiyā, saying: Muḥammad ibn Mālik narrated to us from Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Salama, from Khuṣayf, who said: «الجبت» is the soothsayer, and «الطاغوت» is Satan.
Al-Shaʿbī, ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الطاغوت» is Satan.
Mujāhid said concerning His words ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَحَاكَمُوا إِلى الطَّاغُوتِ﴾: he is "Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf."
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another. The basis of «طاغوت» in the language is taken from ṭughyān (transgression); it conveys its meaning without [strict] derivation, as it is said that al-laʾāl ("pearl-seller") is from al-luʾluʾ.
Sībawayh said: As for «الطاغوت», it is a single feminine noun that applies to the plural.
So according to Sībawayh, when its verb is plural it is taken to refer to the devils, and when singular it is taken to refer to Satan.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the good things said about «الطاغوت» is that it is whoever transgresses against Allah. Its original form is "ṭaghawūt," like jabarūt, from ṭaghā when one exceeds one's limit; then the lām [radical] is transposed and made the ʿayn, and the ʿayn is transposed and made the lām, as in jabadha and jadhaba; then the wāw is changed to alif because it is vowelled and the letter before it is vowelled, so you say: «طاغوت».
And the meaning is: whoever denies the lordship of everything worshipped besides Allah, and believes in Allah.
The basic sense of «الجبت» in the language is that in which there is no good.
Quṭrub said: Its origin is al-jibs, which is the dull, heavy one in whom there is no good.
Abū ʿUbayda said: «الجبت» and «الطاغوت» are everything worshipped besides Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not fall outside what we said. "Muḥammad ibn Yazīd" [al-Mubarrad] differed from Sībawayh regarding his statement that it is a single noun, and said: The correct view in my opinion is that it is a plural.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿فَقَدِ ٱسْتَمْسَكَ بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ﴾, that is, faith.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ﴾ is "There is no god but Allah."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿لاَ ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, "Allah does not change what is in a people until they change what is in themselves"; that is, He does not remove the name of faith from them until they disbelieve.
It is said: faṣamtu al-shayʾa, that is, I broke it.

nahhas-meani:197-197.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ٱلْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَّعْلُومَاتٌ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad informed us: Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Nāfiʿ, the client of Ibn ʿUmar: Did you hear Ibn ʿUmar name the months of ḥajj?
He said: Yes, he used to name Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿda and Dhū al-Ḥijja.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿda and ten [days] of Dhū al-Ḥijja.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The two views come back to one thing, because Ibn ʿUmar named Dhū al-Ḥijja only because the ḥajj is in it, and it is a month of ḥajj.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلْحَجَّ﴾.
Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿUmar said: (فَرَضَ) means he pronounced the talbiya.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās: he entered iḥrām. And it was said: the meaning of "he entered iḥrām" is that he made iḥrām binding on himself by resolve, even if he did not pronounce the talbiya.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its literal meaning in the language is that (فَرَضَ) means he made binding.
The meaning is: he made the ḥajj binding during them by the talbiya [or by intention. And it is possible that its meaning is: whoever made the ḥajj binding on himself by the talbiya] during them, so that the talbiya and the ḥajj are both in them.
And it is possible that the meaning is: whoever made the ḥajj in them binding on himself by a talbiya pronounced in other months.
However, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad informed us: Ibn Jurayj said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ informed me from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "No one ought to enter iḥrām for the ḥajj except in the months of ḥajj, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿ٱلْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَّعْلُومَاتٌ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلْحَجَّ﴾; so no one ought to pronounce the talbiya for ḥajj and then stay on in some land."
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ رَفَثَ وَلاَ فُسُوقَ وَلاَ جِدَالَ فِي ٱلْحَجِّ﴾.
Sufyān ibn Ḥuṣayf [Translator's note: so in the source; probably "Sufyān from Khuṣayf"] related from Miqsam from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «الرفث» is sexual intercourse, «الفسوق» is reviling, and «الجدال» is that you dispute with your companion until you anger him.
Ibn ʿUmar said likewise.
Ṭāwūs related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Zubayr: «الرفث» is innuendo (taʿrīḍ), i.e. that one says: "If we two were not in iḥrām, such-and-such would happen."
ʿAṭāʾ and Qatāda said: «الرفث» is sexual intercourse, «الفسوق» is acts of disobedience, and «الجدال» is that they dispute with one another until one angers the other.
Abū Yaḥyā related from Mujāhid concerning «الجدال» the same as ʿAṭāʾ said.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related [from him]: There is no disputing and no doubt about it [the ḥajj]; and this is the position of Abū ʿUmar ibn al-ʿAlāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the reader meant is Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ].
On that basis he read "رَفَثٌ وَفَسُوقٌ" in the nominative and "جِدَالَ" with a fatḥa.
These views are close to one another, because innuendo about intercourse is a means to it. «الرفث» originally is obscene speech, then it is used as a euphemism for intercourse; and what shows you that it applies to intercourse is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَفَثُ إلى نِسَائِكُمْ﴾.
«الفسوق» in the language is going out from something.
So reviling a Muslim is going out from obedience to Allah.
Ibn Masʿūd related from the Prophet ﷺ: "Reviling a Muslim is wickedness («فسق»), and fighting him is unbelief."
And it was said: the view of ʿAṭāʾ and Qatāda — «الفسوق» is acts of disobedience — is very good.
Moreover, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb related from Yūnus ibn Yazīd from Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿUmar [Translator's note: so in the source; probably "Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar"], who said: «الفسوق» is committing acts of disobedience to Allah in the Sanctuary, i.e. hunting and other things.
This is a comprehensive view, because reviling a Muslim falls within acts of disobedience, as do the things from which only the one in iḥrām is prohibited, and those from which both the one in iḥrām and the one not in iḥrām are prohibited.
The meaning of Mujāhid's saying "no doubt about it" is that it is in Dhū al-Ḥijja; for those who practised intercalation (al-nasaʾa) sometimes placed the ḥajj in other than Dhū al-Ḥijja, and some of them would stand at Jamʿ and some at ʿArafa, and they would dispute about which of that was correct. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Time has come round to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, and the ḥajj is in Dhū al-Ḥijja."
Abū Zayd said: Abū ʿAmr said: He meant: let there be no «رفث» and no «فسوق» in anything that takes one out of the ḥajj.
Then He began the negation anew and said: ﴿وَلاَ جِدَالَ فِي ٱلْحَجِّ﴾.
So he indicated that the first is a prohibition.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.
Sufyān related from ʿAmr from ʿIkrima, who said: "Some people used to come to Mecca for the ḥajj without provisions, so they were commanded to take provisions."
Mujāhid said: The people of Yemen used to say: "Do not take provisions" — and so they would get their way from people [by begging]; so they were commanded to take provisions.
Qatāda said something similar.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.
I.e. it is part of piety (taqwā) that a man not expose himself to the begging that is forbidden to him.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱتَّقُونِ يٰأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾.
I.e. [people of] minds; and the lubb of everything is its pure essence.

nahhas-meani:198-198.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُواْ فَضْلاً مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: al-Ramādī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Sufyān informed us from ʿUmar ibn Dīnār [Translator's note: so in the source; the known narrator is ʿAmr ibn Dīnār], who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Dhū al-Majāz and ʿUkāẓ were markets for people in the Jāhiliyya; when Islam came they disliked that, until there was revealed: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُواْ فَضْلاً مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾ in the seasons of ḥajj.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَإِذَآ أَفَضْتُم مِّنْ عَرَفَاتٍ﴾, i.e. you pour forth.
One says: fāḍa al-ināʾ (the vessel overflowed), when it is full and pours out from its sides.
And a man fayyāḍ, i.e. who gushes with giving.
Zuhayr said:
وَأبْيضَ فَيَّاضٍ يَدَاهُ غَمامةٌ * عَلى مُعْتَفِيهِ ما تُغِبُّ نَوَافِلُهُ
(And a noble, bounteous man whose two hands are a rain-cloud over those who seek his favour; his gifts never fail to come.)
And a ḥadīth mustafīḍ, i.e. one [transmitted] in continuous succession.
Abū al-Ṭufayl related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "ʿArafāt was named so only because Gabriel used to say to Abraham, peace be upon them both: This is the place of such-and-such; and he would say: I know it (ʿaraftu), I already know it; for that reason it was named ʿArafāt."
Al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ and Nuʿaym ibn Abī Hind said something similar.
Ibn al-Musayyab said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Allah sent Gabriel to Abraham, may Allah bless them both, until, [when] he came to ʿArafāt, he said: I already know it. He had come to it before that; and for that reason it was named ʿArafa.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلْمَشْعَرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: What lies between the two mountains is a mashʿar.
Qatāda said: It is Jamʿ. He said: It was named Jamʿ only because the "Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ" prayers are combined (yujmaʿ) there.
Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: remember Him by affirming His oneness, and the meaning is praising Him; ﴿وإِنْ كُنْتُم مِنْ قَبْلِه﴾, i.e. before His guiding [you].

nahhas-meani:199-199.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ﴾.
ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The Arabs used to stand at ʿArafāt, and Quraysh considered themselves too great to stand with them, so Quraysh would stand at al-Muzdalifa; so Allah commanded them to pour forth from ʿArafāt with the people."
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "The people" is Abraham ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first is more fitting.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim from his father, who said: "I went out looking for a camel of mine at ʿArafa, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing at ʿArafa with the people, before he was sent [as a prophet]; and I said: By Allah, this man is one of the Ḥums; what is he doing standing here?"
Abū Jaʿfar said: The Ḥums are those who were strict in their religion; al-ḥamāsa is strictness. [And it is said: "ثُمَّ"] in the language indicates a second after a first, with an interval between them. And Allah the Exalted said, after ﴿فَاذكُروُا الَّلهَ عِنْدَ المَشْعَرِ الحَرَامِ﴾:
﴿ثُمَّ أَفِيْضُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ النَّاسُ﴾.
Yet the pouring forth from ʿArafāt is before coming to the Sacred Mashʿar?
There are two answers to this:
One of them: that (ثُمَّ) has the meaning of the wāw.
The second answer, which is the preferred one: that (ثُمَّ) is in its proper sense, and the meaning is: then you were commanded to pour forth from ʿArafāt from where the people pour forth.
In this there is a meaning of tawkīd (emphasis), because they were commanded to remember [Allah] at the Sacred Mashʿar, and they poured forth from ʿArafāt; then the pouring forth from where the people pour forth — not from where Quraysh used to pour forth — was emphasised to them.
And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الكِتَابَ﴾; and one says: "So-and-so is generous, then [moreover] he looks after us", and "So-and-so fights people, then [moreover] he is vile in himself", i.e. then I tell you more about him.
In the verse there is another good view, according to the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿النَّاسُ﴾ is Abraham, peace be upon him; so the meaning would be: from where Abraham the Friend [of Allah] poured forth, which is the Sacred Mashʿar.
This would be like ﴿الذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ﴾, and that [one] is "Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd al-Ashjaʿī".
It has been related from him that he read: (ثُمَّ أَفَيِضوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أفَاضَ النَّاسِي), meaning Adam; and this is an irregular (shādhdh) reading.

nahhas-meani:200-200.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمْ مَّنَاسِكَكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The shedding of blood [of the sacrifices].
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَآءَكُمْ أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْراً﴾.
Abū Mālik and Abū Ṣāliḥ related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "When the Arabs had completed their rites and stayed at Minā, a man would stand and ask Allah, saying: O Allah, my father had a great feeding-bowl, a great tent, much wealth; so give me the like of what You gave him."
I.e. he does not remember Allah the Exalted; he only mentions his father, then asks to be given [something] in this world.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ آتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمَا لَهُ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلاَقٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: (الخَلاَقُ) is the share. And the believers say: ﴿رّبَنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ — he said: wealth — ﴿وَفِي الآخِرَةِ حَسَنَة﴾ — he said: Paradise.
Hishām said, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿آتَِنَا فِي الدُّنيَا حَسَنةً﴾ — he said: knowledge and worship; ﴿وَفِي الآخِرَةِ حَسَنة﴾ — he said: Paradise.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: Well-being in this world and well-being in the Hereafter.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views come back to one thing: that good and blessing are from Allah.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَقِنَا﴾, i.e. turn away from us.
One says of it: waqaytuhu kadhā, aqīhi, waqāyatan, wiqāyatan and waqāʾan; and it may also be said: waqāka Allāhu waqyan.

nahhas-meani:257-257.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿ٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The darkness is unbelief and the light is faith; unbelief is likened to darkness and faith to light.
It was read to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb [al-Nasāʾī], from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Manṣūr narrating from a man, from ʿAbada ibn Abī Lubāba, concerning this verse: ﴿ٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ﴾ up to His words ﴿هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾. He said: They are people who had believed in ʿĪsā, and when Muḥammad came they disbelieved in him. He said: And there were people who had disbelieved in ʿĪsā, and when Muḥammad came they believed in him; so this verse was revealed about them.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Nasāʾī] said: Jarīr narrated it from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid.
If it is said: What is the meaning of ﴿يُخْرِجُونَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنُّورِ إِلَى ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ when they were never in light at all?
The answer is that it is said: "I saw so-and-so outside the house," even if he had not gone out of it; and "I put him out of the house" means I placed him outside it. Likewise "he brought him out of the light" means he made him be outside it, even if he had not been in it.
And it was said: This is a figurative depiction of what they were turned away from: they were in the position of one who has been put out of it, as it is said: "Why have you put me out of your religion?"
And it was said: since they were born upon the fiṭra (primordial nature) — which is the taking of the covenant and the knowledge of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, upon which they were created — and then disbelieved, they had been brought out of the light.
Al-Akhfash said: ﴿ٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ﴾ means He judges that they are so. You say: "Allah has brought you out of this matter," when you were never in it at all.
Abū Isḥāq said: This is nothing. Rather, He increases them in guidance through their faith; He is their protector (walī) in their argumentation and guidance and in giving them victory over their enemy, and He takes charge of their reward.

nahhas-meani:258-258.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ﴾.
This is the alif of drawing attention (alif al-tawqīf), and the speech carries the sense of wonder, that is: wonder at him!
Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid said: He is Numrūdh ibn Kanʿān.
Sufyān said: He summoned two men, killed one of them and spared the other.
Sufyān said: ﴿فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَ﴾: he fell silent and did not answer him with anything.
And it has been read: ﴿فَبَهَتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ﴾,
that is: Ibrāhīm dumbfounded the one who disbelieved.

nahhas-meani:259-259.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوْ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: It is said that he is ʿUzayr, and the town is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).
﴿فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِئَةَ عَامٍ﴾: the first thing of him to come to life was his head, and he began looking at everything of him that was being created, and at his donkey.
Saʿīd said from Qatāda: It was mentioned to us that ʿUzayr came upon Jerusalem after Nebuchadnezzar (Bakhtanaṣṣar) had laid it waste. He said: So he said: How will this be rebuilt after its ruin?
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِئَةَ عَامٍ﴾.
It was mentioned to us that he died in the forenoon and was raised before sunset after a hundred years, and he said: I have stayed a day or part of a day.
Kaʿb said: He is ʿUzayr.
Mujāhid said: He is a man of the Children of Israel.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: He is Armiyā (Jeremiah), and he was a prophet.
Al-khāwiya is the empty.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says khawat khuwiyyan, khawāʾan and khawāyatan.
Al-ʿurūsh are the roofs, that is, fallen down upon its roofs.
Abū ʿUbayda said: One says: khawat ʿurūshuhā: its houses.
And al-ʿurūsh are tents, which are the houses of the Bedouin.
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: The kāf in His words ﴿أوْ كَالَّذِي﴾ is conjoined to the sense of the speech, that is: Have you seen [anyone] like the one who disputed with Ibrāhīm, or like the one who passed by a town?
And it was said: it is redundant (zāʾida), as He said: ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيءٌ﴾.
* And His words: ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾.
ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: it has not changed.
Mujāhid said: it has not gone putrid.
Some lexicographers said: lam yatasanna is from their saying āsana al-māʾu when water becomes putrid.
Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said: ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾ means it has not changed, from His words ﴿مِنْ حَمَأٍ مَسْنُونٍ﴾; then one of the two nūns was replaced by yāʾ, as is said taqaṣṣaytu and taẓannaytu, and qaṣṣaytu aẓfārī ("I clipped my nails").
Abū Jaʿfar said: Both views are mistaken. Had it been from their saying asina al-māʾu when it becomes putrid, it would be yataʾassan.
Abū Isḥāq said: Nor is it from masnūn, because masnūn means poured out in the shape (sunna) of the ground.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct view is that it is from al-sana (year), that is, the years have not changed it.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ﴾.
Sufyān said from al-Aʿmash: He returned to his sons [to find them] old men while he was young.
Al-Kisāʾī said: The speech is only [complete] by implying (iḍmār) a verb.
The meaning according to him is: We did this in order to make you a proof for people and a sign of Our power; and like it is ﴿وَحِفْظَاً﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱنْظُرْ إِلَى ٱلعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُهَا﴾.
That is, We bring them to life. ﴿ونُنْشِزُهَا﴾ with the dotted zāy means: We set some of the bones upon others and raise some of them onto others.
And al-nashz and al-nashaz are raised ground.
And whoever read: ﴿قَالَ: أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ —
Qatāda said, regarding his reading: he began to look at how some of his bones were joined to others, because the first thing of him to be created was his head, and it was said to him: Look; so he said this about that.
Ṭāwūs narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿قَال اعْلَمْ﴾ as an imperative; that is, it was said to him.
Hārūn said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: ﴿قيل: اعْلَمْ﴾ as an imperative.
And it is also possible that he addressed himself with this.

nahhas-meani:260-260.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِـي ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: the meaning is "that my heart may be at rest through witnessing," as though his soul demanded of him to see that, and when he saw it, it was at rest. A person may know a thing from one direction, then seek to know it from another.
This view is the position of the eminent scholars; it is the position of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan.
Al-Ḥasan said: For the son of Adam, report is not like seeing with one's own eyes.
The other view: the meaning of ﴿وَلَـكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾ is "[that my heart may be at rest] that when I ask You, You answer me,"
as Sufyān narrated from Qays ibn Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ تُؤمِنْ﴾ in the intimate friendship (khulla)? He said: [i.e.] are you not certain of the khulla?
And Abū al-Haytham narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿وَلَـكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾: that it may increase.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ﴾.
ʿAbd al-Bāqī ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Umawī narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr narrated to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿa narrated to us from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Hubayra al-Sabīnī, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ﴾. He said: They are the pigeon, the peacock, the crane and the cock.
Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
"He took the cock, the peacock, the crow and the dove."
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَصُرْهُنَّ﴾ means pluck them, feathers and flesh.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ṣirtu means "I cut," and ṣurtu means "you gathered." [Translator's note: so in the source, «جَمَعْتَ» with the second person.]
And Abū ʿUbayda reported: ṣurtu ʿunuqahu, aṣūruhā, and ṣirtuhā, aṣīruhā: I bent it; and ṣawira [means it became bent].
It is read with ḍamma and with kasra, and most of the readers have ḍamma.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Whoever reads it with ḍamma takes it from ṣurtu al-shayʾa: I inclined it and drew it to myself. He said: and ṣur wajhaka ilayya, that is, turn it toward me.
The meaning on this reading is: draw them to yourself and cut them up; then "and cut them up" was omitted because ﴿ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءَاً﴾ indicates it.
And whoever read ﴿فَصِرْهُنَّ﴾ with kasra, there are two views about it:
One of them: it has the meaning of the first.
The other: Abū Mālik and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: cut them up.
Abū Ḥātim said: It is from ṣāra when one cuts. He said: In that case it involves fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), as though He said: "Take four birds to yourself and cut them up."
Someone else said: From it a herd of wild cattle is called ṣiwār and ṣuwār, that is, it has broken off and gone apart; and for this reason pieces of musk are called aṣwira, as [the poet] said:
"إِذَا تَقُومُ يضُوغ المِسْكُ أَصْوِرَةً"
(When she rises, the musk wafts forth in pods.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting thing said about the meaning of fa-ṣirhunna and fa-ṣurhunna is that they have one meaning, the meaning of cutting, with fronting and postponement, that is: "Take to yourself four birds and cut them up."
And the distinction [between the two] has not been found authentically from any of the early authorities.
﴿ثُمَّ ادْعُهُنَّ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Come, by the permission of Allah!" — so the flesh of this one flew to the flesh of that one. ﴿سَعْيَاً﴾, that is, running on their feet; one does not say of a bird when it flies that it "ran" (saʿā).
﴿وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾, that is, nothing He wills is beyond Him.
﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He arranges.
Then, having related what contains proofs, He urged jihad, and made known that whoever strives after this proof — which only a prophet brings — has in his striving a great reward.

nahhas-meani:261-261.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ up to His words: ﴿وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
That is, Generous: what He bestows of His bounty does not diminish His abundance; ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ (All-Knowing) of where to place it.

nahhas-meani:264-264.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُبْطِلُواْ صَدَقَاتِكُم بِٱلْمَنِّ وَٱلأَذَىٰ﴾.
That is, do not remind [people] of what you have given and count it [as a favour], as though you intend that; and al-adhā (hurt) is that the recipient is reproached.
So He made known that these two nullify charity, just as the charity of the hypocrite who gives to be seen, to give the impression that he is a believer, is nullified.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ﴾, that is, the likeness of his spending, ﴿كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ﴾, which is the smooth rock; and al-wābil is the rain of heavy drops.
﴿فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْدَاً﴾.
Qatāda said: with nothing on it.
And the meaning is: they had no power over their earnings at the time of their need; it was wiped out and taken away, just as the rain takes away the soil on the rock, finding nothing on the rock to hold it in place.

nahhas-meani:202-202.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾.
I.e. He already knows what is in favour of the one being reckoned and what is against him before making him stand for his reckoning; and He reckons with him without needing to recall or deliberate, and the human being is not like that.

nahhas-meani:203-203.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَاتٍ﴾.
I.e. by affirming His oneness and extolling Him; ﴿فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَاتٍ﴾, i.e. counted days.
They were commanded to pronounce the takbīr after the prayers, and at the stoning, with each pebble of the pebbles of the Jamarāt.
Sufyān related from Bukayr ibn ʿAṭāʾ from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Daylī, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The days of Minā are three days, "the days of Tashrīq"; whoever hastens [departure] in two days, there is no sin upon him."
Nāfiʿ related from Ibn ʿUmar: The "known days" and the "counted days" together are four days: the known days are the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, and the counted days are three days after the Day of Sacrifice: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَاتٍ فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلاۤ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيه﴾: he is forgiven.
ʿAṭāʾ, Ibrāhīm, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ فَلاَ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in his hastening, ﴿وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلاۤ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in his delaying.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿لِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: This was made permissible for the hastening of whoever is God-fearing.
So the implied sense on this view is: the permission is for whoever is God-fearing.
Ibn Masʿūd said: It is forgiveness of sins for whoever was God-fearing in his ḥajj.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is like his first view. As for Ibrāhīm's view — ﴿وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلاۤ إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in his delaying — it is a far-fetched interpretation, because the one who delays has reached the utmost, and one does not say [of him]: there is no blame on him.
And it was said: It is possible to say "there is no blame on him", because it is good to take up Allah's concessions; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, made known that there is no sin on him in his not taking up the concessions.
What indicates the soundness of Ibn Masʿūd's view is the ḥadīth of Shuʿba from Manṣūr from Abū Ḥāzim from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever performs ḥajj and does not engage in «رفث» or «فسق» returns as on the day his mother bore him."
The meaning on this view: whoever performs ḥajj and guards in his ḥajj against what diminishes it, there is no sin upon him from past sins.
I.e. the ḥajj has expiated [them] for him.
And the implied sense is: the expiation of sin is for whoever is God-fearing.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: Ḥājib ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated to us from Sumayy from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The accepted ḥajj has no reward but Paradise."
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the saying of Abū al-ʿĀliya: (لا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ): his sin has gone entirely if he fears Allah in what remains, i.e. of his life.

nahhas-meani:204-204.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: [I.e.] his outward [speech]. ﴿وَيُشِهدُ اللَّهَ﴾ in the dispute that what he wants is the right and that he does not seek wrong; ﴿وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلْخِصَامِ﴾: a wrongdoer.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: They are the hypocrites.
Ibn Muḥayṣin read: (وَيُشْهَدُ الَّلهُ) with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ, and the nominative [for the divine name], and its meaning is: and Allah knows.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلْخِصَامِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: I.e. a wrongdoer who does not go straight.
Qatāda said: Intensely argumentative with falsehood.
Al-aladd in the language is one fierce in dispute, derived from al-ladīdān, which are the two sides of the neck.
I.e. whichever side of the dispute he takes, he prevails, as the poet said:
إنَّ تَحْتَ الأحْجَارِ حَزْمَاً وَجودَاً * وَخَصِيمَاً ألدَّ ذَا مِعْلاَقِ
(Beneath the stones lie resolve and generosity, and a fierce adversary who clings fast [in argument].)
And it is also related as "مِعْلاق". And it is said: it is from ladīdā al-wādī, i.e. its two sides.
So the possessor of this description takes one side and leaves uprightness; and al-ludūd is in one of the two sides.
Abū Isḥāq said: al-khiṣām is the plural of khaṣm (adversary).

nahhas-meani:205-205.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ سَعَىٰ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيِهَا وَيُهْلِكَ ٱلْحَرْثَ وَٱلنَّسْلَ﴾.
I.e. when he leaves you, he hastens to the ruin of tillage and offspring.
Abū Mālik related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "It was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq. He went out from the Prophet ﷺ and passed by crops belonging to some Muslims, and donkeys; he burned the crops and hamstrung the donkeys."
Abū Isḥāq related from al-Tamīmī from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «الحرث» is people's tillage, and al-nasl is the offspring of every creature.
Qatāda said: «الحرث» is crops, and al-nasl is the offspring of everything.
Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd informed me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: As for His saying ﴿وَيُهْلِكَ ٱلْحَرْثَ وَٱلنَّسْلَ﴾, [al-nasl] is people and every creature; and as for «الحرث», it is gardens and the growing stock.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close in meaning; and the meaning is: he burns, destroys and kills.

nahhas-meani:206-206.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلْعِزَّةُ بِٱلإِثْمِ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us from Abū Isḥāq from Saʿīd ibn Wahb, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: "It is sin enough for a man that his brother says to him: Fear Allah, and he says: Mind yourself! Are you commanding me?"

nahhas-meani:207-207.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ﴾.
I.e. he sells; and the meaning of selling himself is: expending himself for Allah.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: Ṣuhayb came emigrating towards the Prophet ﷺ, and a band of the polytheists of Quraysh pursued him. He dismounted from his mount, scattered what was in his quiver, took his bow, and said: O company of Quraysh, you know that I am among the best archers of you; and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot what is in my quiver, then struck with my sword as long as anything of it remains in my hand; then do what you will. They said: Show us your house and your property in Mecca, and we will leave you alone.
They made a pact with him and he did so. When he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "Abū Yaḥyā, the sale has profited, [the sale has profited]." So Allah revealed: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: They are the Emigrants and the Helpers.

nahhas-meani:208-208.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱدْخُلُواْ فِي ٱلسِّلْمِ كَآفَّةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means Islam.
Abū Mālik related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is saying: [enter] into Islam altogether.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of al-silm is peace and reconciliation. It is possible that the meaning is: remain firm upon Islam; and it is possible that the meaning is [addressed] to whoever has believed with his tongue.
It has been related that some Jews became Muslim and persisted in holding the Sabbath sacred, so Allah commanded them to enter into all the laws of Islam.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَاتِ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the sins which he commands.
Abū Isḥāq said: I.e. do not follow his tracks, because your abandoning any of the laws of Islam is following Satan.

nahhas-meani:209-209.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَإِن زَلَلْتُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْكُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾.
I.e. you turn aside from the right course.
﴿فَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾: you cannot frustrate Him and nothing frustrates Him; ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He created you upon and laid down for you of His religion.

nahhas-meani:210-210.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي ظُلَلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْغَمَامِ وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Allah will come on the Day of Resurrection in canopies of cloud.
And it was said: ﴿هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ with what He promised them of good deeds [rewarded] and punishment.
﴿فَأَتَاهُمُ اللهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا﴾, i.e. by His forsaking them.
This is the view of Abū Isḥāq.
Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: ﴿أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ means His command.
Because Allah the Exalted does not move from place to place; as you say: "We feared that the Banū Umayya would come to us", meaning only their rule.
﴿وَقُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾, i.e. what they were promised is finished for them.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ ٱلأُمُورُ﴾.
Yet they are returning to Him at every time.
Quṭrub said: The meaning is that the questioning about deeds, and the reward and punishment for them, return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, because today they are not being called to account for them.
Someone else said: In this world there were matters in the hands of people who acted unjustly in them and took what was not theirs; so all of that returns to Allah, and He judges it with truth.
And after it: ﴿وَقُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾, i.e. judgement was decided with justice between creatures.

nahhas-meani:211-211.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿سَلْ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُم مِّنْ آيَةٍ بَيِّنَةٍ﴾.
I.e. confirming the matter of the Prophet ﷺ.
Mujāhid said: What is mentioned of them in the Qurʾān and what is not mentioned. He said: And they are the Jews.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: I.e. disbelieves in it. This was said to them because they altered what was in their scriptures.

nahhas-meani:212-212.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلْحَيَاةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: I.e. Iblīs made it attractive to them, because Allah has urged renunciation of it and made known that it is the enjoyment of delusion.
And it was said: Its meaning is that Allah created pleasing things, and those who disbelieved looked at them as worth more than their measure.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾.
He said: I.e. in respect of what they possess.
Ibn Jurayj said: They mock them for seeking the Hereafter.
Qatāda said: ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ﴾, i.e. in Paradise.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾.
He does not provide for the believer according to the measure of his faith, nor provide for the unbeliever according to the measure of his unbelief.
I.e. He does not reckon provision in this world according to the measure of deeds.
Quṭrub said: The meaning — and Allah knows best — is that He gives [His servants from an allotted thing], not from a number greater than it from which He takes it, like a human giver giving a thousand out of two thousand.
He said: Another aspect is that whoever spends something for which he is not called to account, that is "without reckoning".

nahhas-meani:265-265.t:
He said: ﴿وَمَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَتَثْبِيتاً مِّنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾.
That is, they spend it acknowledging and firmly convinced that it is among what Allah rewards.
Al-Ḥasan said: When he wanted to spend, he would make sure (tathabbata): if it was for Allah, he went ahead; otherwise he held back.
Qatāda said: ﴿تَثْبِيتَاً﴾, that is, seeking reward (iḥtisāban).
Mujāhid said: They make sure where they place their wealth, that is, their zakāt.
Al-Shaʿbī said: [It means] affirmation and certainty.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Had it been as Mujāhid said, it would be "wa-tathabbutan," from tathabbattu, like takarramtu takarruman.
And Qatāda's saying "and seeking reward" is not known [linguistically], unless what is meant is that their souls make them firm while seeking reward; and this is far-fetched.
And al-Shaʿbī's view is good, that is, a strengthening on their behalf from their own souls in spending that in obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It is said: thabbattu fulānan fī hādhā al-amr, that is, I made his resolve sound and strengthened his judgement in it — uthabbituhu tathbītan. That is, their souls are certain and affirming of Allah's promise, upon their making sure in that.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is level, elevated ground; it doubled its fruit.
Qatāda said: ﴿بِرَبْوَةٍ﴾, he says: on a raised piece of ground. He said: This is a parable Allah has struck for the deeds of the believer. He says: his good never fails, just as the good of this garden never fails in whatever state it is: whether "a downpour (wābil) strikes it" — which is heavy rain — or "a drizzle (ṭall)" strikes it.
Mujāhid said: [It is] dew.
And it was said: light rain that lasts.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: That is, the drizzle suffices it.

nahhas-meani:266-266.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ﴾ up to His words: ﴿فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ﴾.
Ibn Abī Mulayka said, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr: ʿUmar asked them about this verse and mentioned it, and they said: "Allah knows best." ʿUmar became angry and said: "Say 'we know' or 'we do not know.'" He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "There is something in my mind about it." He said: "Speak, and do not belittle yourself." He said: "It was struck as a parable for deeds." He said: "Which deeds?" He said: Then ʿUmar said: "This is a man who used to act in obedience to Allah; then Satan was sent to him, and he committed sins, and so burned up [his] deeds."
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās by a chain other than this: This is a parable Allah has struck for those who perform deeds for show; Allah will nullify them on the Day of Resurrection when they are most in need of them — like a man who had a garden and grew old, having small children who could not benefit him; then a whirlwind (iʿṣār) struck the garden — a violent wind containing intense scorching heat (samūm) — and it burned up, so he lost it when he was most in need of it.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: al-iʿṣār is the violent wind.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-iʿṣār is what people call al-zawbaʿa (the whirlwind).

nahhas-meani:267-267.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنْفِقُواْ مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ﴾.
That is, give the good [part] in charity.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Salāma narrated to us, saying: Bakkār narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us from al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik, from al-Barāʾ, who said: "They used to bring the worst of their dates and the worst of their food as charity; so there was revealed: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنْفِقُواْ مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ﴾ up to His words: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تُغْمِضُواْ فِيهِ﴾."
He said: Were it owed to you and he gave it to you, you would not take it except while considering that he had shortchanged you of your due.
Abū Isḥāq said concerning His words ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾: that is, He did not command you to give charity out of [His] need; rather He tested your state, and He is praiseworthy for that and for all His blessings.

nahhas-meani:268-268.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱلْفَقْرَ﴾.
That is, with poverty: he frightens you so that you give the inferior [part] in zakāt. ﴿وَيَأْمُرُكُم بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ﴾: that you not give charity, and so disobey and cut [the ties of kinship] with one another.
﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعِدُكُم مَّغْفِرَةً مِّنْهُ وَفَضْلاً﴾.
That is, that He will requite you for your charity with forgiveness and replacement.
﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
He gives out of abundance, and knows where to place that, and knows the unseen and the seen.

nahhas-meani:269-269.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَن يَشَآءُ وَمَن يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَمَن يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً﴾ — he said: knowledge of the Qurʾān: its abrogating and abrogated [verses], its decisive and ambiguous [verses], what in it comes earlier and later, its lawful and unlawful, and its parables.
Mujāhid said: intelligence, chastity and being correct in speech.
Zayd ibn Aslam said: Wisdom («حكمة») is understanding in the religion of Allah.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Wisdom is the Qurʾān.
Qatāda said: [It is] comprehension.
I say: These views agree. The basic sense of «حكمة» is that by which one is restrained from folly. Knowledge was called «حكمة» because by it one is restrained, and by it restraint from folly is known — folly being every ugly act; and likewise the Qurʾān, intelligence and comprehension.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: [It is] comprehension of the Qurʾān.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلاَّ أُوْلُواْ ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾.
That is, none reflects with a reflection by which he takes heed of the signs He has related except the possessors of intellect, and whoever has understood from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His command and His prohibition.

nahhas-meani:270-270.t:
He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَمَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ مِّن نَّفَقَةٍ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: [That is,] in an obligatory [spending], because He mentioned the charity of zakāt.
﴿أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِّن نَّذْرٍ﴾.
Everything a person intends to do voluntarily is a vow (nadhr).
And it was said: the meaning is: whatever spending you spend without a vow, or [whatever] you vowed and then bound yourselves to spend ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ﴾, that is, it is not hidden from Him, so He will requite it.
Mujāhid said: ﴿يَعْلَمُهُ﴾, that is, He records it.

nahhas-meani:271-271.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿إِن تُبْدُواْ ٱلصَّدَقَاتِ﴾.
That is, if you make them manifest.
And in the ḥadīth: "Secret charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord."
And it was said: This was in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; as for today, people think ill [of those who give secretly].
Al-Ḥasan said: Making zakāt manifest is better, and concealing voluntary [charity] is more excellent, because it is a stronger indication that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone is intended by it.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: This was acted upon by ﴿الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بالَّليْلِ والنَّهارِ سِرَّاً وَعَلاَنِيَةً﴾; then when "Barāʾa" was revealed with the obligation of charity and its details, charity came to rest on that.

nahhas-meani:272-272.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: They used to dislike giving charity to their relatives among the polytheists; then they were granted a dispensation in that, and there was revealed: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ﴾ to the end of the verses.

nahhas-meani:273-273.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِلْفُقَرَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُحصِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the emigrants (muhājirūn) of Quraysh who were in Medina.
Someone else said: The meaning of ﴿أُحصِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is: the obligation of jihad prevented them from going about [earning a living].
And it was said: their enemy kept them busy with fighting from going about [earning a living].
Abū Jaʿfar said: The language requires that (أُحْصِرُوْا) be from illness, except that the meaning may be: they were found in this state.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْباً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It was said: they have bound themselves to jihad, as it is said: "I cannot disobey you," that is, I have bound myself to obeying you.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿يَحْسَبُهُمُ ٱلْجَاهِلُ أَغْنِيَآءَ مِنَ ٱلتَّعَفُّفِ﴾.
Ignorance (jahl) here is not the opposite of intelligence; it is only the opposite of acquaintance (khibra).
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿تَعْرِفُهُم بِسِيْمَاهُمْ لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ إِلْحَافاً﴾.
It is said: alḥafa fī al-masʾala, akhfā and alaḥḥa, with one meaning ("he was importunate in asking"). [Translator's note: «أخفى» is as written; the expected word is «أحفى».]
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever asks while he has forty dirhams has been importunate (alḥafa)."
Abū Isḥāq said: Its meaning is: he has been all-encompassing in asking; and from it liḥāf (a cover) is derived. He said: And the meaning of ﴿لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ إِلْحَافاً﴾ is: no asking comes from them at all, such that there could be importunity, as the poet said:
على لاَ حِبٍ لا يُهْتَدَى بَمَنَارِهِ * إذَا سَافَهُ العَوْدُ النَّبَاطِيُّ جَرْجَرا
(On a well-trodden road whose waymarks give no guidance; when the old Nabataean camel sniffs it, it groans.)
That is, it has no waymark by which one could be guided.

nahhas-meani:213-213.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: Adam [alone] was a single community.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr [Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect Saʿīd (ibn Abī ʿArūba) narrating from Qatāda] related from Qatāda, who said: He is saying: "They were all upon a law of truth."
It was mentioned to us that between Adam and Noah there were ten generations, all of them acting in obedience to Allah, upon guidance and upon the law of truth; then they differed after that, so Allah sent Noah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: (أُمَّة) is from their saying amamtu kadhā, i.e. I made for it (intended it).
So the meaning of (أُمَّة) is that their aim is one; and a solitary person is called an "umma", i.e. his aim is other than the aim of people.
And al-umma is stature, as if it were the aim of the rest of the body; and al-imma — with kasra — is also blessing (niʿma), because people make for it; and imām is so called because people aim at [following] what he does.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ﴾.
I.e. the Book decides by judgement.
Al-Jaḥdarī read: (ليُحْكَم) with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a fatḥa on the kāf.
And al-Farazdaq said:
ضَرَبَتْ عَلَيْكَ العَنْكَبُوتُ بنَسْجِهَا * وقَضَى عَلَيْكَ بِهِ الكِتَابُ المُنْزَلُ
(The spider has spread its web over you, and the revealed Book has decreed it against you.)
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا ٱخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ﴾.
I.e. none differed about the Book except those who were given it.
Abū Isḥāq said: I.e. none differed about the truth of the Prophet's ﷺ matter except those who were given knowledge of its truth, upon him be blessing and peace.
﴿بَغْياً بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, i.e. for the sake of transgression; i.e. they brought about the disagreement only out of transgression.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
Abū Mālik related from Ibn ʿAbbās: The unbelievers differed about it, and Allah guided those who believed to the truth of that.
Abū Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"We are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection; we are the first of people to enter Paradise, except that they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. So Allah guided us to the truth about which they differed. This is the day about which they differed, [and Allah guided us to it], so people follow us in it: tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow for the Christians."
And in a version of the ḥadīth: "Allah guided us to the day of Jumuʿa (Friday)."
Zayd ibn Aslam said: They differed: the Jews took the Sabbath and the Christians Sunday, and Allah guided the community of Muḥammad to Friday.
And they differed about the qibla, and they differed about prayer and fasting: some of them fast from some foods, and some of them fast part of the day.
And they differed about "Abraham", and Allah guided the community of Muḥammad to the truth of that.
Abū Zayd said: And they differed about Jesus: the Jews made him [the fruit of] a calumny, and the Christians made him a lord; and Allah guided the believers.
Abū Isḥāq said: ﴿بإذْنِهِ﴾, i.e. by His knowledge.

nahhas-meani:214-214.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ ٱلْجَنَّةَ﴾.
(أَمْ) here is for moving from one topic to another.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوْاْ مِن قَبْلِكُم﴾.
Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl reported that "مَثَل" may mean "description" (ṣifa).
And the meaning may be: and the like of what befell those before you has not yet befallen you. And (خَلَوْا), i.e. passed away.
﴿مَسَّتْهُم البَأْسَاء والضرَّاء﴾, i.e. poverty and illness.
(وزلْزِلُوا): they were made afraid and shaken by what harms.
Abū Isḥāq said: The origin of al-zalzala is from zalla al-shayʾ ʿan makānihi (the thing slipped from its place); so when you say zalzaltuhu, its meaning is: you repeated its slipping from its place.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مَعَهُ مَتَىٰ نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ﴾? [verse 214].
I.e. strain reached them to the point that they thought the help slow in coming.
And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّ نَصْرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ﴾, i.e. He will help His friends without fail.

nahhas-meani:215-215.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾? [verse 215].
I.e. give in charity and give.
﴿قُلْ مَآ أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِّنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَٱلأَقْرَبِينَ وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
It was said: They had asked on whom they ought to bestow [their bounty].
So it was said: The most deserving of those on whom bounty is bestowed are these.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
I.e. He counts it, and when He has counted it He requites it.

nahhas-meani:216-216.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ﴾.
Most of the exegetes hold that jihād is obligatory, and that the meaning is: fighting has been made obligatory for you, except that some of them suffice in place of others.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وقاتِلُوا في سَبيلِ الله﴾.
Abū Ṭalḥa said concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿انْفِروُا خِفَافَاً وَثِقَالاً﴾:
I have not heard that Allah excused anyone.
However, Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Jihād is voluntary, and the meaning of ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ﴾ is [prescribed] in the sense of its being meritorious.
Then He said: ﴿وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: The interpretation is: and it is a thing of aversion to you. [One says:] karihtu al-shayʾ kurhan, karhan, karāhatan and karāhiyatan.
Al-Kisāʾī said: It is as if al-kurh is from yourself, and al-karh — with a fatḥa — is what you are compelled to.
﴿وَعَسَىٰ أَن تَكْرَهُواْ شَيْئاً وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
I.e. if he is killed he is a martyr, and if he kills he is rewarded and takes booty, and he demolishes the cause of unbelief, and by fighting brings about the entry into Islam of those he fights.
﴿وَعَسَىٰ أَن تُحِبُّواْ شَيْئاً﴾: staying back from fighting.

nahhas-meani:217-217.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلشَّهْرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ قِتَالٍ فِيهِ قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: Fighting in it was a grave matter — as He, Exalted is He, said — then it was abrogated in Barāʾa: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوا المُشْرِكين كَافَّة كَمَا يُقَاتِلونَكُم كافَّةً﴾.
Abū al-Sayyār related from Jundab ibn ʿAbd Allāh that the Prophet ﷺ sent out a party and put over them Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith — or ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith. When he went to set off, he wept out of longing for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; so he sent "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh" instead, wrote a letter for him, and ordered him not to read the letter until he reached such-and-such a place, and said: Do not compel your companions to go on.
