When he reached the place he read the letter, said "To Allah we belong and to Him we return", and said: Hearing and obedience to Allah and His Messenger. He said: Two men went back, and the rest of them went on. They met al-Ḥaḍramī and killed him, not knowing that that day was of Rajab. The polytheists said: You have killed in the sacred month. So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلشَّهْرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾ — the verse.
And it was said: [They said:] If we have not incurred a burden of sin, then there is no reward for us either. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمنوا والَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا في سَبِيلِ اللهِ﴾ to the end of the verse.
Mujāhid said: ﴿قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ﴾, i.e. grievous.
And the sentence is complete [there]. Then He began anew and said: ﴿وَصَدٌّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ﴾, i.e. in Allah, ﴿وَٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾, i.e. and barring from the Sacred Mosque;
﴿وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ﴾, meaning the Sacred Mosque, ﴿أَكْبَرُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ than killing in the sacred month.
﴿وَٱلْفِتْنَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ ٱلْقَتْلِ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: I.e. unbelief; and the meaning is: these deeds of yours [O polytheists] are unbelief, and unbelief is graver than killing in the sacred month.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَن دِينِكُمْ إِن اسْتَطَاعُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the unbelievers of Quraysh.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أُوْلۤـٰئِكَ يَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
And what is the meaning of ﴿يَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ when He has already praised them?! [The answer is] that they do not know with what [end] their lives will be sealed.

nahhas-meani:274-274.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Mujāhid informed us from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ سِرّاً وَعَلاَنِيَةً﴾; he said: "It was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. He had four dirhams with him, and he spent one dirham by night, one dirham by day, one dirham secretly and one dirham openly."

nahhas-meani:275-275.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَا لاَ يَقُومُونَ إِلاَّ كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ مِنَ ٱلْمَسِّ﴾.
The meaning is: ﴿ٱلَّذِيْنَ يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَا﴾ in this world ﴿لاَ يَقُومُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿إِلاَّ كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ مِنَ ٱلْمَسِّ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, madness.
Someone else said: This is a mark for them on the Day of Resurrection. People will come out of their graves hurrying, as He the Exalted said: ﴿يَخْرُجوْنَ مِنَ الأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعَاً﴾ — except those who devour usury (ribā): they rise and fall. Allah will swell the usury in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection until it weighs them down, so they get up and fall, wanting to hurry but unable.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَمَن جَآءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِّنْ رَّبِّهِ فَٱنْتَهَىٰ﴾.
Sufyān said: He means the Qurʾān.
And the meaning of ﴿فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ﴾ is: it is forgiven him.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: That is, Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is his guardian.
Someone else said: ﴿وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾ in His protecting him and granting him success: if He wills, He protects him from consuming it, and if He wills, He forsakes him in that.
Some exegetes said: ﴿وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِِ﴾ in the future.
This is a good and clear view, that is: his affair is with Allah in the future; if He wills He keeps him firm upon the prohibition, and if He wills He makes it permissible.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.
Sufyān said: whoever returns and practises usury until he dies.
Someone else said: whoever returns and says "Trade is only like usury" has disbelieved.

nahhas-meani:278-278.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَذَرُواْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ ٱلرِّبَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: In the Jāhiliyya, a man would be owed a debt by another man, and [the debtor] would say: "You get such-and-such and you defer [payment] for me"; so he would defer it for him and he would give him more.

nahhas-meani:279-279.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾.
That is, be certain. It is said: adhintu bi-l-shayʾ, so I am adhīn bihi ("I am assured of it"), as [the poet] said:
* "فَإِنِّي أَذِينٌ إنْ رَجَعْتُ مُمَلَّكَاً" *
(For I am pledged/assured, if I return as one made king…)
And the meaning of "fa-ādhinū" [with the long vowel] is: inform others that you are at war with them.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُؤُوسُ أَمْوَالِكُمْ لاَ تَظْلِمُونَ وَلاَ تُظْلَمُونَ﴾.
Then al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: In the Jāhiliyya they used to trade with usury; then Islam came while they still had wealth [outstanding], so they were commanded to take their capital and not take the usury with which they had charged interest, and they were commanded to give in charity to whoever was in hardship.

nahhas-meani:280-280.t:
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيْسَرَةٍ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: It was revealed concerning usury.
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham said: It is for every one in hardship: he is granted respite.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is good, because the reading in the nominative (marfūʿ) means: "and if there occurs one in hardship" among all people — if among those you claim from or trade with there is one in hardship. [Translator's note: i.e. kāna here is complete (tāmma), "occur, be".]
Had it been about usury specifically, the accusative (naṣb) would have been the [proper] way, meaning: "and if the one who owes the usury is in hardship."
However, al-Muʿtamir narrated from Ḥajjāj al-Warrāq that in the codex of ʿUthmān [it is]: "وَإِنْ كَانَ ذَا عُسْرَة"; and the meaning is: then upon you is respite (naẓira), that is, deferral until he becomes well off.
And it is narrated from ʿAṭāʾ that he read "فَنَاظِرَةٌ إِلَى مَيْسَرَةٍ" by way of command.
[Translator's note: «فناظرة» is as written; the reading usually attributed to ʿAṭāʾ is «فناظِرْهُ», an imperative, which fits "by way of command".]
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَن تَصَدَّقُواْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: that is, with the capital.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: And that you give in charity from the capital is better than respite.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: "Ibn ʿAbbās held that the last verse of the Qurʾān to be revealed was ﴿وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمَاً تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إلَى اللهِ﴾."
It was read to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, who said: My father narrated to me from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمَاً تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إلَى اللهِ﴾ — the verse — that it is the last verse revealed to the Messenger of Allah, upon him be peace.

nahhas-meani:283-283.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِن كُنتُمْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُواْ كَاتِباً فَرِهَانٌ مَّقْبُوضَةٌ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read "كتاباً" (a writing).
And he said: A scribe may be found while no sheet is found.
Abū al-ʿĀliya, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Mujāhid read likewise.
And it was said: kitāb is the plural of kātib, as one says qāyim [Translator's note: so written, for qāʾim] and qiyām.
And it was said: they [i.e. the two readings] are equivalent.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَرِهَانٌ مَّقْبُوضَةٌ﴾.
It has been read "فَرُهُنٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ"; ruhun is the plural of rihān, and it may be the plural of rahn, like saqf and suquf.

nahhas-meani:219-219.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْخَمْرِ وَٱلْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْخَمْرِ وَٱلْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ﴾; then He revealed: ﴿لاَ تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأنْتُم سُكَارَى حَتَّى تَعْلَموا ما تَقُولونَ﴾ [so they used to leave it off]; when they had prayed the ʿIshāʾ they would drink it, and by morning the intoxication would have left them; and when they had prayed the morning prayer they would drink it, and by the time of Ẓuhr the intoxication would have left them. Then some people drank it and fought one another and spoke what does not please Allah; so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿إنَّما الخمرُ والميسرُ، والأنْصَابُ، والأَزْلامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَل الشَّيْطانِ، فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ﴾.
So Allah forbade wine, prohibited it, and commanded that it be shunned, just as He commanded that idols be shunned.
Abū Tawba related from Ibn ʿUmar: ﴿إنَّما الخَمْرُ﴾ was revealed, up to His saying ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُم مُنْتَهونْ﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: It has been forbidden.
ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl said: ʿUmar said: We have desisted, for it takes away wealth and reason.
The exegetes hold that this is what made it forbidden.
Some jurists said: What made it forbidden is two verses:
One of them: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما حَرَّمَ رَبّي الفَواحِشَ ما ظَهَر مِنْها وما بَطَنَ وَالإثْم﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: Wine is this [drink] agreed upon; and the analogy for everything that does what it does is that it be called wine and be in its position in prohibition. For the scholars agree that all gambling is forbidden, yet He mentioned only maysir among it, so all of it was made analogous to maysir — and maysir is gambling over slaughter-camels specifically; likewise everything that is like wine is in its position.
The interpretation of khamr in the language is: what covers the mind. Everything of trees and the like that covers a person is called khamar, and what covers him of trees specifically is al-ḍarā, with a short final alif.
And [one says] "he entered into the khumār of the people", i.e. into the great crowd in which one is concealed.
A woman's khimār is her veil, because it covers [the head]; and the khumra is what one prostrates on, because it screens the face from the ground. And every intoxicant is khamr, because it mixes with the mind and covers it; and so-and-so is makhmūr from any intoxicant.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said: maysir is all gambling.
As for the sin in wine, it is enmity and hatred, and that it comes between a person and his reason by which he discerns and knows what is owed to his Creator.
And gambling breeds enmity, because a person's property passes to another without any return that he receives for it.
And the benefits: the pleasure of wine and the profit in [trading] it, and something coming to a person in gambling without toil.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Their benefits were before the prohibition, and their sin after the prohibition.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَ؟ قُلِ ٱلْعَفْوَ﴾.
Ṭāwūs said: A little of everything.
Khālid ibn Abī ʿImrān said: I asked al-Qāsim and Sālim, and they said: The surplus of wealth: what is given in charity out of sufficiency.
Qatāda said: It is the surplus.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views come back to one thing, because al-ʿafw in the language is what is easy.
One says: "Take what has become easy (ʿafā) for you", i.e. what is easy for you.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "The best charity is what is given out of sufficiency."
On this basis is the interpretation of the view of al-Qāsim and Sālim. And there is another view on the meaning:
Mujāhid said: It is the obligatory alms; but the apparent sense points to the first view.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ يُبيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ [verses 219–220].
Abū Jaʿfar said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shabīb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Maʿmar informed us from Qatāda concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
He said: He is saying: that you may reflect on this world and the Hereafter, and so know the superiority of the Hereafter over this world.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied sense according to Qatāda's view is: that you may reflect on the affair of this world and the Hereafter.
And it was said: It involves advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), i.e. thus Allah makes clear to you the signs concerning the affair of this world and the Hereafter, that you may reflect.

nahhas-meani:220-220.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ قُلْ إِصْلاَحٌ لَّهُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When there was revealed ﴿إِنَّ الذَّينَ يَأْكُلونَ أَمْوَالَ اليَتَامى ظُلْماً﴾ to its end, they said: This is a binding [threat]; so they kept apart from them and abandoned mixing with them. That was hard on them, and they said to the Prophet ﷺ: The sheep have been left with no herdsman, and the food with no one to prepare it. So there was revealed: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ قُلْ إِصْلاَحٌ لَّهُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾ to its end.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ٱلْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِ﴾.
I.e. He knows who mixes with them in order to betray, and who does not intend betrayal.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: I.e. had He willed, He would not have permitted you to mix with them in food and pasture.
Al-Ḥakam related from Miqsam from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ اللَّهَ لأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾ — he said: had He willed, He would have made what you enjoyed of the orphans' property a cause of ruin.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿لأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾: He would have destroyed you.
Abū Isḥāq said: Its literal sense is: He would have charged you with what is hard on you, so that you would fall into hardship.
He said: The origin of al-ʿanat in the language is from their saying "ʿanita al-baʿīr ʿanatan", when a break occurs in its leg after it has been set, so that it cannot use it.
﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾, i.e. He does by His might what is required, and no one can avert it from Him.
﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾: possessed of wisdom in what He commanded you concerning orphans and other matters.

nahhas-meani:221-221.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ حَتَّىٰ يُؤْمِنَّ﴾.
Most scholars hold that this verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿اليَوْمَ أُحِّلَ لَكُمُ الطَّيِبَّاتُ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَالمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الَّذِيِنَ أُوتُوا الكِتَابِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾.
This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Makḥūl, and it is the position of the jurists "Mālik, Sufyān and al-Awzāʿī".
Sufyān related from Ḥammād: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about marrying a Jewish or Christian woman, and he said: There is no harm in it. He said: I said: But Allah says: ﴿وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ حَتَّىٰ يُؤْمِنَّ﴾. He said: [That is] the idolaters and the Magians.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda: ﴿وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ﴾ — he said: the polytheist women who are not of the People of the Book; and Ḥudhayfa married a Jewish or a Christian woman.
As for ﴿المُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبلِكُم﴾, it was said: they are the chaste women, and the slave women.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تُنْكِحُواْ ٱلْمُشِرِكِينَ حَتَّىٰ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾.
I.e. do not marry them to Muslim women; ﴿وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ﴾, i.e. even if his affair in this world pleases you, his destination is the Fire.
﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
I.e. they do the deeds of its people; so your offspring would be raised with one whose state is this.
﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَدْعُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
[I.e. He calls you to the deeds of the people of Paradise.]
﴿وَالمَغْفِرَة بِإذْنِهِ﴾.
It was said: I.e. by His knowledge; i.e. what He called you to is a means of reaching them.
And it was said: by what He commanded you; ﴿وَيُبَيِّنُ آيَاتِهِ﴾, i.e. His signs.
﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾: so that they may be in hope of taking heed.

nahhas-meani:222-222.t:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْمَحِيضِ قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى﴾.
Qatāda said: I.e. filth.
Thābit related from Anas (that when a woman menstruated, the Jews would put her out of the house, and would not eat with her, nor drink with her, nor keep company with her in a house. The Prophet ﷺ was asked about that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْمَحِيضِ قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى، فَٱعْتَزِلُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فِي ٱلْمَحِيضِ﴾ — the verse. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Keep company with them in the houses, and do everything except intercourse."
So by this ḥadīth the meaning of ﴿فَٱعْتَزِلُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فِي ٱلْمَحِيضِ﴾ becomes clear: its meaning is: keep away from them in intercourse only.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ حَتَّىٰ يَطْهُرْنَ﴾.
I.e. until the blood stops for them.
The people of Kufa read: ﴿يَطَّهَّرْنَ﴾, i.e. they wash themselves.
And likewise is the meaning of ﴿يَتَطَهَّرْنَ﴾, which Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy read.
Some people found fault with ﴿يَطْهُرْنَ﴾ — without doubling — saying: because touching is not lawful until they have washed.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not follow; for its meaning may be like the meaning of ﴿يطَّهَّرْنَ﴾, and its meaning may be: until it becomes lawful for them to purify themselves, as one says of a divorced woman when her waiting period has ended: she has become lawful for men. And He made that clear by His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا تَطَهَّرْنَ﴾.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَأَتُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: From where they were forbidden it during their menstruation.
Ibrāhīm said: In the vagina.
Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya said: By way of marriage, by way of the lawful.
Abū Razīn said: By way of purity.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: ﴿ويُحِبُّ المُتَطَهَّرِيَن﴾ from sins.
ʿAṭāʾ said: With water.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of ʿAṭāʾ is more fitting, because of the ḥadīth that the Prophet ﷺ said — to the people of the Mosque of Qubāʾ —: "Allah has praised you well in [the matter of] purification; will you not tell me [why]? They said: O Messenger of Allah, we find it written for us in the Torah: cleansing [after relieving oneself] with water."
And this was when there was revealed: ﴿فِيهِ رِجَالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَتَطَهَّروُا﴾.

nahhas-meani:282-282.t:
The words of Him, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
1- Among them: that this is by way of recommendation (nadb), not an absolute requirement.
2- Among them: that Abū Naḍra narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that he recited this verse, ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ﴾, until he reached ﴿فَإنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضَاً فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي ائْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ﴾, and said: This verse abrogated what preceded it.
3- And it was said: this [writing] is obligatory for deferred [transactions], and witnessing for immediate ones; the dispensation is only in [the matter of] the pledge (rahn).
It is said: dāyantu al-rajula when I lent to him and borrowed from him; and likewise tadāyana al-qawmu ("the people dealt in debts with one another").
Adantu al-rajula: I sold to him on credit; and dintu and iddantu mean I took on credit; and I am dāʾin and muddān.
And al-mudīn is the king, when people submit (dāna) to him, that is, hear and obey.
Among the questions asked is: What is the point of "بِدَيْنٍ" when "تَدَايَنْتُمْ" already indicates debt — can there be mutual debt-dealing without a debt?
The answer is that the Arabs say "tadāyannā," meaning "we requited one another" and "we exchanged taking and giving"; so "بِدَيْنٍ" came to make the intended meaning clear.
And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌ بِٱلْعَدْلِ﴾.
Al-Suddī said: with truth, that is, he does not write for the creditor more than what is his, nor less.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
It was said: as Allah has taught him of writing with justice.
And it was said: as Allah has favoured him with the knowledge of writing.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَإن كَانَ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهاً أَوْ ضَعِيفاً أَوْ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ﴾.
Ibn Wahb said: Yūnus informed me that he asked Rabīʿa: What is the description of the safīh (feeble-minded)?
He said: The one who does not make his wealth grow in his selling and buying, and does not deny himself any pleasure; he falls upon wealth as one who regards wealth as nothing; the one who is not seen to have any sense regarding wealth.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The safīh is the one ignorant of dictation, and the ḍaʿīf (weak) is the clumsy.
Abū Isḥāq said: The safīh is the one light of intellect; and from this: tasaffahat al-rīḥu al-shayʾa, when the wind moves a thing and makes it light; and from it:
مَشَيْنَ كَمَا اهْتَزَّتْ رِمَاحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ * أَعَالِيَهَا مَرُّ الرَّياح النَّواسِمِ
(They walked swaying as spears sway whose tops are tossed by the passing of gentle breezes.)
Someone else reported that safah is everything whose doing is ugly, that is, it is an act that is not well-made, from their saying thawb safīh when a garment is loosely woven.
As for the ḍaʿīf, he is — and Allah knows best — one in whom there is weakness, from muteness, senility or madness.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of this:
Sufyān narrated from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The guardian of the safīh is the one whose management of his affair is valid for him; he is his walī, that is, he takes charge of his affair; ﴿بِالعَدْلِ﴾: he is the one who dictates the right [owed].
[Translator's note: al-Ḥasan's explanation is not given in the source after the chain; the text moves straight to al-Ḍaḥḥāk.]
And the other view, from Ibn ʿAbbās, is that the meaning is: let the guardian of the one to whom [the right] is owed dictate.
[Translator's note: «وليّ الذي هو عليه» is translated as written, "the one to whom it is owed"; literally «عليه» would be "upon whom"; the known view of Ibn ʿAbbās is "the guardian of the creditor (walī al-ḥaqq)".]
This view was used as an argument by those who hold that there is no interdiction (ḥajr) on free, adult, sane persons; this is the position of Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَٱسْتَشْهِدُواْ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ﴾.
It was said: from the people of your religion.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ﴾.
That is, of those whose way of life you approve.
Ibrāhīm said: of those in whom no cause for suspicion has appeared.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿أَن تَضِلَّ إْحْدَاهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا ٱلأُخْرَىٰ﴾.
That is, that one of them should forget, so the other reminds her.
And it is narrated from al-Jaḥdarī: ﴿أنْ تُضِلَّ﴾, that is, she is made to forget, as is said: unsītu kadhā ("I was made to forget such-and-such").
As for what is narrated from Ibn ʿUyayna, that he said: [The other one] makes their testimony equivalent to the testimony of a male (dhakar) — the lexicographers do not know it, and it is also a mistake, because if its meaning were only "We make her equivalent to a male," there would be no need for "أَنْ تَضِلَّ", since she would make her equivalent to a male whether she forgot or not.
And it is not possible that she makes her equivalent to a male when she has forgotten her testimony.
As for the fatḥa of "أَنْ", we will mention it in [our book on] the iʿrāb, if Allah wills.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُواْ﴾.
Ibn Najīḥ [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere Ibn Abī Najīḥ] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: When he is called to testify having already been made a witness.
Al-Ḥasan said: And when they are called initially to [bear] witness, and they should not refuse when called to give it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It was said: al-Ḥasan's view is more likely, because if that [refusal] were [allowed] to them, rights would be lost; and because after it comes ﴿وَلاَ تَسْأَمُوۤاْ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيراً أَو كَبِيراً إِلَىٰ أَجَلِهِ﴾, that is, do not grow weary of writing down the right, be it much or little, as it is said: "I will certainly give you your right, be it small or great."
Al-Akhfash said: ﴿أَنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ﴾ — so he implied (aḍmara) the witness; he said: and He said ﴿إلَى أَجَلِهِ﴾, that is, until the term in which his testimony is valid. And Allah knows best.
This is in the words of al-Akhfash verbatim.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] chose the view of Mujāhid: that the meaning of ﴿وَلاَ يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُواْ﴾ is that, when you hold a testimony and are called; and this is the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima, al-Shaʿbī and al-Nakhaʿī.
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: "Because Allah has given them the name 'witnesses' (shuhadāʾ), and the name 'witnesses' only applies to them if they have witnessed something before that; it is not permissible that they be called 'witnesses' when they have not witnessed.
Were that so, all people would be witnesses, in the sense that they [can] witness. So the meaning becomes: when they are called to give the testimony. Moreover, the entry of the alif and lām shows that the one intended by the prohibition is a known person."
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْومُ لِلشَّهَادَةِ﴾.
Sufyān said: Its meaning is "more just." Then He said ﴿وَأقْومُ لِلشَّهَادَةِ﴾, that is, more firmly established, because the document reminds the witness of what he witnessed.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَدْنَىٰ أَلاَّ تَرْتَابُوۤاْ﴾.
That is, that you do not doubt.
Then He granted a dispensation to leave off writing in what frequently passes between people, and He the Exalted said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ﴾.
* And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلاَ يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلاَ شَهِيدٌ﴾.
There are several views on it:
1- Among them: the meaning — according to the view of ʿAṭāʾ — is: let them not refuse when they are called.
As Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrima, who said:
ʿUmar used to read "وَلاَ يُضَارِرْ كَاتِبٌ ولا شَهِيدٌ" (with kasra: let no scribe or witness cause harm).
Ṭāwūs said: Let no scribe cause harm by writing what was not dictated to him.
Al-Ḥasan said: And let the witness not cause harm by adding to his testimony.
2- And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid: ﴿وَلاَ يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلاَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ — they said: It was forbidden that one should come to the witness and the scribe and call them to writing and witnessing while they are busy, and so harm them, saying: "Allah has commanded you not to refuse," while he has no need of them.
The implied construction (taqdīr) on this view is "وَلاَ يُضَارَرْ" (with fatḥa: let no scribe or witness be harmed), and so Ibn Masʿūd read.
So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, forbade this, because had He left it unrestricted, it would distract them from the affairs of their religion and their livelihood.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِن تَفْعَلُواْ فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ﴾.
Sufyān said: ﴿فَإنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ﴾ — he said: disobedience.

nahhas-meani:284-284.t:
The words of Him, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِن تُبْدُواْ مَا فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
There are several views on it:
It is narrated from Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās that it is abrogated by His words ﴿لاَ يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفْسَاً إلاَّ وُسْعَهَا﴾.
Except that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: It was not abrogated; rather, when Allah gathers the creatures He will say: "I will inform you of what you concealed within yourselves." As for the believers, He will inform them and then forgive them.
As for the people of doubt and suspicion, He will inform them of the denial they concealed; that is His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
And it is His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾, of doubt and hypocrisy.
Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: Maḥmūd ibn Ghaylān informed us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us from Ādam ibn Sulaymān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿وَإنْ تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ الله﴾, something entered their hearts from it that had not entered them before. The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: We hear, we obey and we submit. So Allah cast faith into their hearts, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ — the verse — and revealed ﴿لاَ يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفْسَاً إِلاَّ وُسْعَهَا، لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ [رَبَّنَا لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنَا إنْ نَسِينَا أوْ أَخْطَأْنَا]﴾ — He said: I have done so — ﴿رَبَّنَا وَلاَ تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إصْرَاً كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا﴾ — He said: I have done so — ﴿رَبَّنَا وَلاَ تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لاَ طَاقَةَ لَنا بِهِ، واعْفُ عَنَّا، واغْفِرْ لَنَا، وَارْحَمْنَا، أَنْتَ مَوْلانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى القَوْمِ الكَافِرينَ﴾ — He said: I have done so."
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated from al-Shaʿbī, who said: "It was abrogated by the verse after it: ﴿لا يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفْسَاً إِلاَّ وُسْعَهَا﴾."
Miqsam narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: It was revealed concerning testimony, that is, concerning disclosing and concealing it.
Mujāhid said: This is about doubt and certainty.
Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Umayya, that she asked ʿĀʾisha about this verse, ﴿وَإِن تُبْدُواْ مَا فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ﴾, and asked her about this verse, ﴿مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءَاً يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾. ʿĀʾisha said: No one has asked me about them since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about them, and he said: "O ʿĀʾisha, this is Allah's reproaching the servant through what befalls him [of fever, misfortune and the thorn-prick — even the goods he puts in his sleeve] and then misses, and is alarmed for it, then finds it in his armpit; until the believer comes out of his sins as red gold comes out of the bellows."
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "Allah will inform him on the Day of Resurrection of what he used to keep secret, so that he may know that it was not hidden from Him."
And it was said: There can be no abrogation in this, because it is a statement of fact (khabar); rather, it is explained by ﴿إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبَائِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾.
So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: whether you disclose what is within yourselves or conceal it, of the major sins. And what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās is good; and Allah knows best what He meant.
As for what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding abrogation, it is among the things whose interpretation must be considered carefully, since abrogating and abrogated do not occur in reports (akhbār).
If it is authentic, its interpretation is that the second is like the first, as you say: "I copied (nasakhtu) this from this."
And another view was stated about it, whose meaning would be: so what had mixed with their hearts of that was removed, and [the matter] was made clear.
